title: Choose the Atlassian integration substrate and credential boundary
description:
## Question

Given the completed API, ACLI, Jira, Confluence, and ResourceFS architecture research, should ResourceFS use a native REST client, an ACLI-backed adapter, or a deliberately split implementation? Decide the credential source and lifecycle for one operator-owned account per named site, optional dependency behavior, multiple-site isolation, and the evidence that makes the choice reversible or final.

notes.content:
Resolution

ResourceFS will use a native REST implementation: Jira REST v3 and Confluence REST v2, retaining v1 only for CQL search where v2 has no equivalent. This destination includes no ACLI adapter, fallback, transport interface, or runtime dependency. The choice is final for this destination. Reconsider ACLI only through a new decision if official ACLI gains Confluence coverage, versioned machine schemas, pagination/header/error access, request-scoped site isolation, and acceptable distribution/support terms.

One `atlassian` Source Adapter configuration owns multiple validated named sites. Each site independently owns its target URL and explicit OAuth cloud ID where applicable, one credential, grants, caches, and product probes. Jira and Confluence are enabled and marked required or optional independently, so one degraded product does not disable a healthy sibling or another site.

Each site selects exactly one typed authentication variant. There is no automatic fallback and no product-specific principal within a site.

- API-token authentication contains the Atlassian account email and a token `SecretReference`. ResourceFS resolves it during check/probe/launch, retains it only in process memory, and picks up rotation on restart.
- OAuth authentication contains the expected cloud ID and a configured direct-argv token-provider command. The provider owns authorization, client secrets, refresh-token persistence, and refresh-token rotation. It emits strict bounded JSON containing only `accessToken` and `expiresAt`. ResourceFS validates the result, single-flights provider calls per site, refreshes before expiry, and never lets provider output determine site authority.

Credential failure is localized. At launch, an authentication failure fails the process when either affected product is required; otherwise the affected products for that site are degraded. At runtime, refresh failure makes that site's products return `source_unavailable` until a later bounded refresh succeeds. ResourceFS never uses an expired credential or silently changes authentication mode. Secrets, provider output, and provider diagnostics remain redacted, while healthy sites continue operating.

Evidence: `research/atlassian-substrate@cf02c0f` shows native APIs expose the complete authoritative Jira/Confluence contract while official ACLI lacks published Confluence support and stable continuation/header/schema/site-isolation guarantees. `research/atlassian-resourcefs-architecture@fdfb19a` shows the compiled adapter, shared HTTP, strict profile, secret-reference, probe, and degraded-source seams can carry this design without adding a second source convention.
Closed: Native substrate, credential lifecycle, multi-site isolation, failure behavior, and reconsideration gates are decided.

title: Read deployment-qualified PR Fact Resources
description:
## What to build

Deliver PR /facts with native identity, actual head/base SHAs and repository/fork availability through the existing source interface and real MCP path. Establish the owned envelope, bounded single-read controls, structured failures and validated deployment configuration through this usable PR read, not a schema-only foundation.

User stories covered: 1–9, 28, 30–31, 34–43. Shared applicable safety/proof stories are included in every slice. Story 44 is the approved breakdown/publication process, not an implementation feature.

Source: GitHub Fact Resource contract specification in the sibling resourcefs-wt-github-resource-contract documentation worktree (docs/github-resource-contract-spec.md). User approved this eight-slice breakdown and dependency graph. Exact grammar/schema spellings marked PROPOSED remain subject to the specification's applicable design approval gate; issue creation does not waive that gate or authorize live tenant operations.

Shared contract (mandatory for every applicable path): existing public SourceAdapter/SourceResource; owned versioned /facts JSON, not private wire DTOs or Markdown scraping; unchanged human projections and five tools. ResourceFS owns acquisition; Cyril owns capture authorization/totals, retention, UI and review meaning. One configured deployment, explicit repository/fork/origin authority, embedder-supplied origin-bound credentials, new Path Session on principal change, REST 2022-11-28, validated selected ghe.com web/API pairing; no new sign-in flow or provider framework.

Preserve deployment/source identity, supplied native repository/object IDs and links, requested versus observed immutable operands, acquisition interval and REST version, supplied upstream versions/times separately, missing/null/unknown values and explicit coverage. VersionTag hashes representation bytes, not Git identity. Reuse the first slice's reviewed envelope and error vocabulary; additive optional fields permitted, unsupported major versions rejected. Keep one ResourceError with stable categories and bounded sanitized structured status/access ambiguity/retry/limit details; no message parsing, hidden-404-to-empty or denial-to-expired-login inference.

Per-read measurement targets: 10 physical attempts including parent lookups/revalidation/retries; 30 seconds shared across send/body/wait; 8 MiB per response; 16 MiB cumulative accepted response bodies; 16 MiB serialized JSON INCLUDING provenance/outcome/continuation; 4 MiB decoded regular-file bytes; 1,000 records per collection. Positive lower-only acquisition controls are separate from display limits: reject zero/above-hard-ceiling inputs and intersect valid requests with operator policy. These are not memory or wire-traffic guarantees. Measure implementation feasibility; do not silently raise ceilings. Reuse bounded retry/cache behavior and honor applicable rate guidance within the same deadline; failed revalidation cannot return stale success.

Collections admit whole verified pages only if all record/body/serialized budgets fit. Ordinary later failures preserve valid earlier pages with honest coverage, and continuation ONLY when valid; continuation is NOT required for retention. First failure without usable data is typed failure, not empty success. Cancellation or authority/requested-identity violations reject the current component including acquired pages. Continuations are credential-free, session-scoped and resource/operand/authority-bound; best-effort traversal, not snapshots. Expose provider caps separately; no invented recovery or exhaustive fallback to hide caps.

## Placement / boundaries

resourcefs-core owns validated PR/reference identity and necessary source-neutral read-control/error integration. resourcefs-sources owns GitHub configuration, private decoding, acquisition and fact projection using the existing HTTP substrate. resourcefs-mcp owns profile/CLI/schema mapping and protocol rendering. Extend SourceAdapter/SourceResource; no GitHub HTTP dependency in core, wire DTO export, sign-in flow or whole-PR coordinator. Keep shared entrypoints thin; extract internal behavior only as needed by this working path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR facts retain native PR/repository IDs and links, actual base/head SHAs and owning repositories. Deliberately distinct fork/base/head/synthetic-merge fixtures cannot be conflated; null/deleted fork metadata is not replaced by the base repository.
- [ ] Finalize reviewed envelope/schema evolution and structured-error conventions for later slices. Preserve missing versus null/empty, unknown provider values, acquisition versus upstream time/version, and VersionTag semantics.
- [ ] Validate trusted SUBDOMAIN.ghe.com and api.SUBDOMAIN.ghe.com pairing before credentialed requests; conflicts/denied repositories cause zero egress. Retain currently supported public-GitHub configuration; no multi-deployment registry or GHES assumption.
- [ ] First-request access-hidden/permission/rate/malformed/limit failures have stable categories and sanitized typed details; parent reads/retries/revalidation consume the same attempt/deadline budget.
- [ ] Independently exercise legacy unpaged pr://owner/repo/number/diff: upstream sees Accept: application/vnd.github.diff, complete valid UTF-8 native diff bytes return exactly, and truncated bodies are refused. File-patch/tree-comparison checks cannot substitute; mutable PR diff is not fixed-revision evidence.
- [ ] Complete this Resource path through validated addressing, configured Source Adapter acquisition/projection, catalog grammar/examples, applicable profile/CLI schema/check integration, public library consumption and real MCP read/recovery. No private inspector, new tool/provider trait or duplicate HTTP client.
- [ ] Independently observe expected upstream requests, requested/observed identities, zero forbidden egress and zero remote writes, including failure/retry/cancellation. Exercise applicable exact/over-limit controls, shared attempts/deadline, sanitized errors, partial retention and integrity overrides. Existing human reads retain their meaning.
- [ ] Library consumers parse complete bounded JSON; real MCP Recovery References reconstruct exactly acquired JSON before parsing. Source continuation is separately upstream acquisition under ADR-0006, not recovery of omitted output.
- [ ] Add applicable ignored live_* read-only smokes for new adapter and primary real rfs stdio paths, gated by RFS_LIVE=1 and GITHUB_TOKEN, skipping cleanly when absent. Record executed evidence and exact revision in the owning issue evidence record; use public/authorized controlled upstream shapes and invariants, not moving counts. Skipped rows are not passes.
- [ ] Run the repository-owned complete verification gate on the final implementation; record live proof separately. Actual numerical enforcement, deadline/transport and allocation behavior require implementation measurements, not inherited synthetic-probe claims. ResourceFS acceptance does not close Cyril corporate ghe.com/native Windows/credentials/storage/UI acceptance.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately (subject to the applicable design approval gate).

title: https:// reads return an upstream error page as a successful Resource
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What is wrong

`HttpsSource` never looks at the upstream status. `read_https` (`crates/resourcefs-sources/src/https.rs`) takes `BoundedHttpResponse::body()` for `:raw` and `ReaderModeDocument::markdown()` otherwise, and `search` uses the reader-mode rendering the same way; `ReaderModeDocument` carries `status` but nothing consults it. A real `404` page is therefore rendered and returned as a successful Resource with its own Version Tag, and can be searched and retained as a Recovery Reference.

Found by the live HTTPS smoke (`crates/resourcefs-sources/tests/https_live_smoke.rs`, row H4): `https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/book/no-such-page-for-resourcefs.html` read 859 bytes of rendered "Page not found" as content. The permanent fixtures never serve a non-2xx document to the HTTPS source, so the deterministic suite could not see it.

The rfs-g2z9 spec is explicit: "An upstream 404 is `not_found`" (spec.md, generic edge dimensions). Other statuses follow the machine-signal vocabulary already used by the GitHub adapter: `401`/`403` are `permission_denied`, `404`/`410` are `not_found`, every other non-2xx (including `429` and `5xx`) is `source_unavailable`. No response body text is matched or echoed.

## Fix shape

Classify `status` in `HttpsSource` for the raw read, the reader-mode read, and search, before any body is treated as content; add a fake-upstream status matrix row to the permanent HTTPS contracts; keep the live H4 row as the real-world witness.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A `404`/`410` from an allowlisted origin returns `not_found`; `401`/`403` return `permission_denied`; `500`/`503`/`429` return `source_unavailable`; no error carries body text.
- [ ] `:raw`, reader-mode reads, and `rfs_search` over the same reference all classify identically.
- [ ] A permanent fake-upstream contract covers the matrix and the live smoke row H4 passes against a real 404.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: HttpsSource::classify_status maps 401/403 -> permission_denied, 404/410 -> not_found, other non-2xx -> source_unavailable on raw, reader-mode, selected reads and search before any body is content. Fenced by crates/resourcefs-sources/tests/https_status_contract.rs (7-status matrix with positive control) and the live row H4 in https_live_smoke.rs, which passes against the real 404 that found it.

title: Harden reader-mode extraction and probe diagnostics
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

Tier-3 findings from the xhigh code review of rfs-g2z9 increment B (2026-08-23). None is a security bypass or silent-data-loss defect (those were fixed in the increment); each is a correctness or hygiene gap worth closing before HTTPS is exercised widely.

1. **Escape Markdown metacharacters in extracted output.** Neither push_text nor href_of escapes; a page containing '# Not a heading' renders as a real heading, '- item' becomes a bullet, '|' merges into adjacent table rows, and hrefs containing parentheses or link text containing ']' emit malformed links. Because this output is the canonical byte string a content-derived Version Tag hashes, an upstream page currently controls ResourceFS's document structure, not merely its content.

2. **Emit a GFM table delimiter row.** Table rows are pushed as separate blocks joined by a blank line, so no renderer treats them as a table — the reader gets pipe-punctuated paragraphs. Also remove State::in_cell, which is written by both the td/th start and end arms and never read.

3. **Give probe failures a diagnostic.** connect_policed collapses resolution failure, policy refusal, and connect failure into a bare false, and SourceProbe::probe passes None into the ProbeDiagnostic slot that exists for exactly this. An operator who set allowPrivateNetwork: false sees Degraded with no explanation and will chase a firewall instead of their profile. AGENTS.md's silent-failure discipline requires distinguishing these.

4. **Resolve ProbeEndpoint.** It is defined and re-exported but never constructed; NetworkProbe::new still takes positional (String, u16, AddressPolicy) tuples whose third element's meaning is carried only by position. Either thread the newtype through or delete it — AGENTS.md names this case directly.

5. **Fix final_url.** It re-parses a Url that is already a Url, and its unwrap_or_else fallback would report the requested URL as the final URL after a redirect chain, silently attributing a document to the wrong origin. response.url().clone() is cheaper and total.

6. **Reattach a detached doc comment.** The block documenting policy_error_or's error-chain walk sits above cancelled_mid_request, so rustdoc renders that function with two unrelated descriptions while policy_error_or ships undocumented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extracted Markdown escapes metacharacters so upstream text cannot inject document structure; golden fixtures cover heading, bullet, pipe, backtick, bracket, and paren cases in both text and hrefs.
- [ ] A table renders as a GFM table with a delimiter row; in_cell is gone.
- [ ] A probe refusal names its cause through ProbeDiagnostic, and a withheld private-network grant is distinguishable from an unreachable host.
- [ ] ProbeEndpoint is either threaded through NetworkProbe::new or deleted; no unused public API remains.
- [ ] final_url is total and returns the response's own URL.
- [ ] rustdoc renders policy_error_or with its own documentation.

title: Implement Atlassian Cloud Jira and Confluence Portable Sources
description:
## Problem Statement

ResourceFS users cannot currently address Jira Cloud issues or Confluence Cloud pages through the same path-shaped interface they use for workspace files, HTTPS documents, GitHub objects, and Path Session artifacts. Agents must switch to product-specific tools, learn unrelated schemas, materialize oversized responses inline, and lose ResourceFS guarantees around canonical identity, bounded recovery, stable errors, credential isolation, Version Tags, and mutation preconditions.

Operators also lack one strict way to configure several Atlassian Cloud tenants, enable Jira and Confluence independently, control create and update authority by container, diagnose required versus degraded products, and rotate credentials without leaking them. A fake-only integration is insufficient because Atlassian pagination, permissions, validators, representations, and response shapes vary in ways only a real tenant can prove.

## Solution

Add one compiled Atlassian Source Adapter that owns `jira://` and `confluence://` Resources for multiple configured Atlassian Site Mounts. It will use native Jira REST v3, Confluence REST v2, and Confluence REST v1 only for CQL. It will reuse ResourceFS's existing Source Adapter, shared HTTP, Server Profile, discovery, Path Session, mutation, error, bounded-result, and recovery interfaces rather than adding ACLI or a second network stack.

Delivery is staged into four independently gated releases. Behavior Contract 1.2.0 provides API-token-authenticated read-only Jira and Confluence Resources, browse collections, and native JQL/CQL Query Resources. OAuth provider-command authentication follows as a separately proven credential variant. Behavior Contract 1.3.0 enables full replacement of existing authoritative Fields. Behavior Contract 1.4.0 adds strict Creation Targets. Every release remains honest about what is supported, carries deterministic contract coverage, updates its public documentation atomically, and satisfies its required real-tenant evidence gate before shipment.

## User Stories

1. As a ResourceFS operator, I want to configure multiple Atlassian Site Mounts in one Server Profile, so that one server can expose several Cloud tenants without identity collisions.
2. As a ResourceFS operator, I want every Site Mount to have a validated lowercase Site ID, so that Jira and Confluence references remain short, stable, and unambiguous.
3. As a ResourceFS operator, I want duplicate Site IDs and duplicate tenant authority rejected, so that one upstream object cannot acquire two canonical ResourceFS identities.
4. As a ResourceFS operator, I want to enable Jira and Confluence independently for each Site Mount, so that I expose only the products I intend to serve.
5. As a ResourceFS operator, I want each enabled product marked required or optional, so that launch behavior matches its operational importance.
6. As a ResourceFS operator, I want a failed required product probe to fail launch, so that automation does not mistake an incomplete server for a healthy one.
7. As a ResourceFS operator, I want a failed optional product to become degraded without disabling healthy products or Site Mounts, so that partial outages remain localized.
8. As a ResourceFS operator, I want API-token credentials supplied through an account email and SecretReference, so that secrets do not live directly in the profile.
9. As a ResourceFS operator, I want API-token rotation picked up on restart, so that credential ownership remains explicit and predictable.
10. As a ResourceFS operator, I want OAuth added later through a typed provider-command credential variant, so that provider-owned refresh state remains outside ResourceFS.
11. As a ResourceFS operator, I want OAuth access-token refresh single-flighted per Site Mount, so that concurrent requests do not stampede the provider.
12. As a ResourceFS operator, I want expired, revoked, or unrefreshable OAuth credentials localized to the affected Site Mount products, so that healthy mounts continue operating.
13. As a ResourceFS operator, I want `rfs check --probe` to report per-product health without printing credentials, so that I can diagnose configuration safely before serving.
14. As an agent, I want `rfs://` and product catalogs to advertise configured Jira and Confluence namespaces without network egress, so that I can discover available Resources cheaply.
15. As an agent, I want to read a Jira project by stable ID, so that navigation does not depend on a mutable display key.
16. As an agent, I want to read Jira project and issue keys as explicit aliases, so that human-facing references remain convenient without becoming canonical identity.
17. As an agent, I want an alias read to return the stable-ID canonical reference, so that later caches, continuations, mutations, and Version Tags use one identity.
18. As an agent, I want Jira issue Aggregates rendered as deterministic Markdown, so that issue metadata and visible fields are readable without product-specific rendering tools.
19. As an agent, I want every visible Jira issue field exposed as an independently addressable Field Resource, so that I can inspect exact native values and mutate only authoritative Fields later.
20. As an agent, I want ordinary Jira field values exposed as canonical JSON, so that semantically identical object-member ordering does not churn Version Tags.
21. As an agent, I want Jira rich-text values exposed as complete ADF JSON, so that unsupported or unknown native members are not lost.
22. As an agent, I want Jira issue comments exposed as distinct Aggregates with authoritative body Fields, so that comment identity, visibility, authorship, and body authority remain separate.
23. As an agent, I want to browse configured Jira projects, project issues, site issues, and issue comments, so that I can navigate without writing JQL.
24. As an agent, I want to execute exact native JQL through a site-scoped Query Resource, so that ResourceFS does not reinterpret Jira query semantics.
25. As an agent, I want enhanced JQL continuations treated as opaque typed state, so that pagination does not depend on guessed token structure.
26. As an agent, I want Jira query results kept in upstream order, so that caller-authored `ORDER BY` remains authoritative.
27. As an agent, I want Jira browse collections sorted deterministically by stable ID, so that fixed navigation is repeatable.
28. As an agent, I want eventual JQL consistency disclosed rather than hidden by synthetic reconciliation, so that I do not mistake a query result for an immediate write snapshot.
29. As an agent, I want to read a Confluence space by stable ID and use a space key only as an alias, so that canonical identity survives key changes.
30. As an agent, I want Confluence page titles excluded from identity, so that renaming a page does not create a different Resource.
31. As an agent, I want Confluence page Aggregates rendered as deterministic Markdown, so that current content and metadata are readable through the normal ResourceFS interface.
32. As an agent, I want current Confluence title and body exposed as authoritative Field Resources, so that later replacement uses exact native content rather than Markdown conversion.
33. As an agent, I want Confluence storage bodies preserved byte-for-byte as UTF-8 storage representation, so that whitespace and unknown constructs round-trip without loss.
34. As an agent, I want current and historical Confluence versions readable with native version metadata, so that history remains navigable without treating native version numbers as public Version Tags.
35. As an agent, I want historical page versions immutable, so that a read of history cannot accidentally become a mutation target.
36. As an agent, I want page ancestors and direct child Pages exposed as collections, so that I can navigate hierarchy without conflating unsupported child content types.
37. As an agent, I want unsupported Confluence child types reported with their native type and ID, so that they are visible rather than silently dropped or promoted into generic Resources.
38. As an agent, I want footer comments, inline comments, and replies exposed as distinct Resources, so that discussion kinds, parentage, and navigation remain accurate.
39. As an agent, I want inline selection, match, resolved, and dangling state readable as metadata, so that the authoritative body Field remains exact and uncluttered.
40. As an agent, I want to browse spaces, pages, hierarchy, and comments, so that common Confluence navigation does not require CQL.
41. As an agent, I want to execute exact native CQL through a site-scoped Query Resource, so that ResourceFS does not invent a cross-product query language.
42. As an agent, I want Confluence cursor and Link continuations validated and hidden behind typed Resource references, so that raw upstream URLs never become public authority.
43. As an agent, I want bounded collection pages capped at 1,000 records and ten upstream requests, so that one tool call cannot consume unbounded network or memory resources.
44. As an agent, I want fixed upstream request sizes appropriate to each endpoint, so that pagination load is predictable across tenants.
45. As an agent, I want collection failure to be atomic, so that a failed later page is never presented as a complete partial collection.
46. As an agent, I want omitted rendered content recoverable through immutable artifact Resources, so that ResourceFS never silently drops successful output.
47. As an agent, I want the next upstream page named separately when artifact recovery hides it, so that ADR-0006 continuation behavior remains usable for Atlassian collections.
48. As an agent, I want `rfs_search` to remain regex or PCRE2 search over rendered Resources, so that native JQL/CQL and ResourceFS content search remain distinct.
49. As an agent, I want Atlassian `rfs_glob` attempts rejected explicitly, so that unsupported discovery never returns a misleading empty result.
50. As an agent, I want each native Field Version Tag derived from the exact bytes ResourceFS exposes, so that replacement preconditions name authoritative content.
51. As an agent, I want Aggregate Version Tags derived from rendered Markdown but rejected as mutation preconditions, so that readable projections cannot masquerade as write authority.
52. As an agent, I want one bounded retry for safe idempotent reads when Atlassian supplies valid retry guidance, so that brief rate limits can recover without unbounded waiting.
53. As an agent, I want retry waits confined to the original logical deadline, so that a retry cannot silently extend a tool call.
54. As an agent, I want repeat reads revalidated through session-local ETags when available, so that caching saves bytes without serving stale content.
55. As an agent, I want an unconditional fetch when no usable validator exists, so that undocumented cache behavior never becomes authority.
56. As an agent, I want stable ResourceError categories for reference, query, permission, absence, limits, source, conflict, mutation, and cancellation failures, so that automation does not parse Atlassian prose.
57. As an operator, I want error messages limited to allowlisted diagnostic fields, so that tokens, account email, provider output, request bodies, queries, cookies, and raw upstream responses cannot leak.
58. As an agent, I want a Jira or Confluence object omitted by upstream permissions to remain outside the visible graph, so that ResourceFS does not claim tenant completeness.
59. As an operator, I want create and update grants narrowed from adapter to Site Mount, product, and stable project or space, so that upstream permissions never imply ResourceFS Mutation Policy.
60. As an agent, I want an existing Jira Field replaced only with one complete native value and a current Version Tag, so that updates do not synthesize incremental or workflow operations.
61. As an agent, I want Jira comment replacement limited to the body Field, so that visibility and other metadata cannot change accidentally.
62. As an agent, I want Confluence page title or body replacement to preserve the companion Field and required native envelope, so that changing one Field cannot erase unrelated page state.
63. As an agent, I want Confluence page and comment writes to use the current native version plus one, so that ResourceFS honors Atlassian's versioned update contract.
64. As an agent, I want mutations revalidated immediately before egress and serialized by the upstream object being changed, so that local callers cannot race each other through stale state.
65. As an agent, I want Jira's external-writer race limitation disclosed, so that compare-before-write is not misrepresented as an atomic CAS guarantee.
66. As an agent, I want proven stale content reported as `version_conflict` and unproven failures reported as `source_unavailable`, so that conflict classification remains evidence-based.
67. As an agent, I want uncertain post-send mutation outcomes returned without guessed content, references, or tags, so that I can reconcile upstream state safely.
68. As an agent, I want to create one Jira issue under a stable project Creation Target, so that project authority comes from the path rather than caller-supplied duplicate fields.
69. As an agent, I want to create Jira comments under a stable issue with complete ADF and optional native visibility, so that parentage and body representation are explicit.
70. As an agent, I want to create one Confluence page under a stable space with an optional stable parent page, so that page identity and hierarchy are validated.
71. As an agent, I want to create footer comments, inline comments, and replies through kind-specific Creation Targets, so that selection and parent requirements cannot be confused.
72. As an agent, I want remote Creation Targets to require an operationId bound to the exact target and submitted bytes, so that concurrent and repeated requests are deterministic within one Path Session.
73. As an agent, I want a successful creation receipt to contain only the validated canonical stable-ID reference, so that I must read the created Resource for authoritative content and Version Tag.
74. As an agent, I want malformed or unsupported native mutation documents rejected before egress as `invalid_mutation`, so that invalid input cannot create an uncertain remote side effect.
75. As an agent, I want Aggregate mutation, Markdown-to-native replacement, hashline editing, delete, move, transition, and metadata mutation rejected explicitly, so that unsupported operations never look successful.
76. As a maintainer, I want real local-TLS fake-upstream contracts for every route and error branch, so that deterministic CI catches protocol and authority regressions.
77. As a maintainer, I want public stdio contracts to exercise profile, probe, launch, catalog, read, search, write, recovery, and errors, so that adapter correctness reaches the shipped interface.
78. As a maintainer, I want ignored read-only live rows against a disposable tenant, so that real pagination, parent links, representations, validators, and auth behavior cannot drift unnoticed behind green fakes.
79. As a maintainer, I want controlled one-off write probes under API-token and OAuth credentials before mutation releases, so that real scope, response, version, and visibility behavior is evidenced without making permanent live tests destructive.
80. As a tenant administrator, I want an idempotent manifest-driven fixture bootstrap and cleanup command independent of ResourceFS mutation code, so that live evidence has a reproducible external oracle.

## Implementation Decisions

- One compiled Atlassian Source Adapter owns both product schemes and any number of configured Atlassian Site Mounts. It reuses the existing Source Adapter, shared HTTP, profile, discovery, Path Session, mutation, and MCP interfaces. There is no dynamic plugin, ACLI subprocess, fallback client, or second egress-policy layer.
- Jira uses native REST v3, including enhanced JQL search. Confluence uses REST v2 for spaces, pages, hierarchy, versions, and comments, retaining REST v1 only for CQL because v2 has no CQL endpoint.
- Delivery has four honest release boundaries: API-token read-only behavior at Behavior Contract 1.2.0; OAuth provider-command authentication without a Behavior Contract bump unless tool-visible behavior changes; existing authoritative Field modification at 1.3.0; and Creation Targets at 1.4.0. Each release updates directly affected documentation, schemas, and tests atomically and is not advertised before its evidence gate passes.
- One consolidated ADR records the native multi-site adapter, rejection of ACLI and separate product adapters, shared-seam reuse, and read-first staging. ADR-0006 continues to govern source continuation alongside artifact recovery.
- An Atlassian Site Mount binds one unique 1–63 byte lowercase Site ID to one Cloud tenant, one selected credential mode, independent Jira and Confluence enablement/requiredness, product health, grants, and cache namespaces. Site IDs begin and end alphanumeric and permit internal hyphens only.
- Authentication is a strict tagged sum. Release 1 accepts only API-token authentication with account email and token SecretReference. Release 2 adds an OAuth provider-command variant with expected cloud ID, strict bounded access-token JSON, expiry, direct-argv execution, provider-owned refresh persistence, and single-flight refresh. No dormant OAuth fields are accepted in Release 1.
- Duplicate tenant authority is invalid. API-token mounts compare canonical site origins; OAuth mounts compare explicit cloud IDs. A credential never appears in identity, cache keys, Version Tags, diagnostics, artifacts, logs, or structured/text tool output.
- Jira project, issue, comment, and field IDs; Jira project/issue aliases; Confluence space, page, comment, and version IDs; and Site IDs are distinct validated domain types. Jira stable IDs are canonical nonzero decimal strings without narrowing to a machine integer. Confluence IDs are exact bounded opaque strings.
- Jira project and issue keys and Confluence space keys are read-only aliases. Alias reads validate the returned stable object and publish its canonical stable-ID reference. Aliases never identify mutation targets, caches, locks, continuations, snapshots, search records, or Version Tags. Page titles are never identity.
- Canonical Jira navigation includes product and Site Mount roots; project collections and stable project Resources; project-key aliases; site/project issue collections and stable issue Resources; issue-key aliases; issue field indexes and Fields; issue comments, comment bodies, and issue/comment Creation Targets. Native JQL Query Resources use `jira://<site>/search/<canonically-percent-encoded-jql>`.
- Canonical Confluence navigation includes product and Site Mount roots; space collections and stable space Resources; space-key aliases; site/space page collections and stable page Resources; current title, body, and version; historical versions; ancestors and direct child Pages; footer/inline comments, body Fields, replies, resolved metadata; and page/comment/reply Creation Targets. Native CQL Query Resources use `confluence://<site>/search/<canonically-percent-encoded-cql>`.
- Every path segment rejects empty values, controls, literal or encoded separators, dot segments, malformed percent encoding, reserved Creation Target collisions, and values above its domain ceiling. Percent-encoded values have one normalized spelling. Upstream responses are untrusted and must revalidate Site Mount authority, stable identity, parent/container ownership, representation, and collection membership before becoming Resources.
- Product roots, Site Mount roots, catalogs, and completion derive from validated configuration and current health without Atlassian egress. Network-backed collections and Query Resources fetch only within their owning Site Mount; no query fans out across sites.
- Site Mount, project, issue, space, current page, historical page version, and comment Aggregates are read-only deterministic Markdown. Aggregates link collections and Fields rather than inlining independently paginated comments. Stable IDs, aliases, authors, timestamps, ownership, parentage, visibility, inline selection, resolution, and dangling state remain metadata.
- Every visible Jira issue value is a Field Resource containing one canonical JSON value. Ordinary values use JSON content type; ADF values use the Atlassian ADF JSON content type. Canonical encoding is RFC 8785-style: object ordering and insignificant whitespace are normalized while null, empty, numeric, array, object, and unknown native members remain distinct.
- Current and historical Confluence body Fields and comment body Fields contain exact storage-format UTF-8 with the Confluence storage content type. ResourceFS never normalizes storage whitespace, converts through rendered HTML, or uses Markdown as mutation authority. Historical Fields remain read-only.
- Deterministic local renderers convert supported ADF and Confluence storage constructs to Markdown. Unsupported well-formed constructs produce typed markers at source position plus projection warnings and a reference to the authoritative Field. Malformed native content fails atomically rather than returning a partial projection.
- The plain-text read envelope includes a Content Type line matching structured output. Authoritative Field bytes contain no ResourceFS frontmatter, so content copied from a Field is valid replacement input.
- Field Version Tags hash exactly the exposed canonical JSON/ADF or exact storage UTF-8 bytes. Aggregate Version Tags hash returned Markdown and are never accepted for mutation. Native Confluence version numbers are private adapter preconditions/readable metadata, not public Version Tags.
- Fixed browse collections sort by stable ID, except hierarchy collections sort by child position then stable ID. Native JQL/CQL results preserve upstream order and make no repeatable-order promise without caller-specified ordering. Missing optional metadata remains explicitly absent rather than becoming empty/default.
- Jira enhanced JQL uses opaque `nextPageToken` and terminal response state. Offset endpoints use validated typed offsets. Confluence follows validated cursor/Link state. Public continuations never expose raw upstream URLs and validate site, product, endpoint family, and query ownership.
- One logical collection page stops at 1,000 records, ten upstream requests, or the upstream terminal marker. Jira list/search requests use 100 items. Confluence v2 collections use 250, page-version calls with `body-format` use 50, and CQL uses 100 without body expansion. Smaller documented or response-reported endpoint maxima win. A failure on any followed page fails the logical page atomically.
- Existing ResourceFS limits and ADR-0006 apply. If rendered output fits, `continuationReference` names the next typed source page. If output spills, `continuationReference` walks the artifact chain and `sourceContinuationReference` separately names the next source page.
- `rfs_search` remains Rust-regex/PCRE2 search over the explicit rendered Resource. `rfs_glob` remains unsupported for Atlassian. Query syntax validation is owned by Atlassian; ResourceFS validates encoding, ownership, and bounds but does not parse JQL or CQL.
- Only idempotent reads may retry automatically, including POST used solely for enhanced-JQL search. One logical operation gets at most one retry after a retryable transport failure or a 429/503 with valid `Retry-After`. Both delta-seconds and HTTP-date are accepted; 0–250 ms jitter and the retry must fit the original deadline. Other rate headers are bounded diagnostics only and never extend or trigger waiting.
- Successful GET responses may be retained only inside the Path Session when they carry an echoable ETag. Every repeat revalidates. A matching-generation 304 may reuse the exact cached response. No usable validator causes an unconditional fetch; unusable validators degrade to absence; a 304 without a matching entry is `source_unavailable`. POST query results are not cached.
- Successful and Unknown mutations invalidate the affected Site Mount product cache namespace, including direct, collection, and query entries. Jira search remains eventually consistent; ResourceFS does not inject reconciliation into later queries.
- Launch-time required/optional product health follows the existing profile contract. OAuth refresh failure remains degraded until a later bounded refresh succeeds. Ordinary rate, transport, and 5xx failures are request-local; there is no background health worker or circuit breaker.
- Stable errors use typed status and response structure, never message matching. Local reference/continuation errors are `invalid_reference`; native query validation is `invalid_pattern`; malformed native mutation input is `invalid_mutation`; 401, ordinary 403, and egress-policy refusal are `permission_denied`; 404/410 are `not_found`; 413/local ceilings are `limit_exceeded`; rate-signaled 403, 429, 5xx, transport failures, malformed upstream authority, unexpected redirects, and unproven conflicts are `source_unavailable`; proven stale authority is `version_conflict`; cancellation is `cancelled`.
- Diagnostics may include Site ID, product, endpoint family, category, HTTP status, normalized retry delay, and a bounded printable request/trace ID from an explicit allowlist. Bounded structured validation details are allowed only for `invalid_pattern` and `invalid_mutation`. Raw response prose, full URLs, request bodies, JQL/CQL text, credentials, provider output, authorization/cookie headers, and account email are never disclosed.
- Mutation Policy narrows monotonically from adapter to Site Mount to product to stable project/space. Create and update are independent; omitted grants are false; delete grants are rejected. Atlassian permissions and OAuth scopes never imply ResourceFS authority.
- Release 3 permits only full replacement of existing authoritative Fields through `rfs_write(path, content, ifVersion)`. Jira sends one complete field set or comment-body replacement. Confluence page title/body replacement uses a whole-page update that preserves the companion Field and required envelope and supplies current native version plus one; comment replacement changes body only.
- All mutations serialize by the upstream object actually written. Immediately before egress, the adapter performs an uncached authoritative load, revalidates identity/container/grants/current capability, derives the current public Field tag, and rejects a mismatch as `version_conflict`. Jira provides local serialization plus immediate compare-before-write but no claim of atomic protection from an external writer.
- Mutation requests never follow redirects or retry. Authoritative success requires a validated response or one uncached refetch. Once a request may have reached Atlassian, missing, malformed, inconsistent, or unrefetchable authority is an Unknown `source_unavailable` outcome with reconciliation guidance and no guessed reference or Version Tag.
- Release 4 adds Creation Targets. Reading `/new` is zero-egress and returns the local contract, grant requirements, operationId rule, and receipt shape. Creation writes accept exactly one strict UTF-8 JSON object; duplicate, unknown, reserved, malformed, over-limit, wrong-representation, and dynamically invalid fields fail before egress.
- Jira issue creation is project-scoped and requires `issueTypeId` plus `fields`, with optional `parentIssueId`; project/type/parent cannot be overridden inside fields. Jira comment creation is issue-scoped and accepts complete ADF body plus optional native visibility.
- Confluence page creation is space-scoped and accepts non-empty title, exact storage body, and optional stable parent page in the same space. Footer comments and replies accept a body. Top-level inline comments additionally require text selection, zero-based match index, and positive match count; inline replies accept body only.
- Remote creation requires `operationId`; `ifVersion` is forbidden. The Path Session journal binds exact submitted bytes and target, coalesces concurrent identical requests, replays completed success, returns `version_conflict` for conflicting reuse, permits retry after conclusive failure, and blocks reissue after Unknown. There is no upstream marker or cross-session deduplication claim.
- A successful creation receipt contains only the validated canonical stable-ID reference. The caller reads the created Resource or Field for authoritative content and Version Tag.
- Atlassian Aggregates never mutate. Atlassian Fields do not support `rfs_edit`, hashline PUT/CUT, REM, or MV. Delete, transition, hierarchy move, owner/status change, historical-version mutation, inline-comment resolution, bulk mutation, properties, and arbitrary upstream update operations remain unsupported.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests defend observable contracts, boundaries, invariants, state transitions, precedence, and real error outcomes. They do not assert private helper calls, internal DTO layout, incidental allocation strategy, or entire Markdown snapshots when stable identity/content invariants suffice.
- The highest user-visible seam is the real `rfs` binary over stdio: strict profile loading, `check --probe`, launch, catalog, tool schemas, `rfs_read`, `rfs_search`, bounded recovery/continuation, later `rfs_write`, text/structured parity, stable categories, redaction, and reported Behavior Contract version. Prior art is the existing stdio MCP contract and stdio live-smoke suites.
- The Source Adapter seam with the existing real local-TLS fake upstream proves exact Jira/Confluence routes, query parameters, headers, request bodies, page transitions, ETags, Retry-After handling, zero egress, cancellation, parent/identity validation, grants, cache invalidation, mutation preflight, idempotency, and Unknown outcomes. Prior art is the GitHub adapter, GitHub mutation, shared HTTP substrate, and HTTP bounds contract suites.
- A narrow source-local native-wire seam proves production-shaped Jira/Confluence JSON, required versus optional/null fields, exact native IDs and parent links, ADF/storage fidelity, malformed authority rejection, bounded diagnostics, and decode budgets. Prior art is the GitHub native-wire contract. Test-only inspection remains behind test support and does not become a production interface.
- The profile/check/probe/launch seam proves strict tagged authentication, multi-site collision checks, independent required/optional products, grants, SecretReference handling, static versus network checks, degraded recovery, credential redaction, source catalogs, and mount construction. Prior art is the profile corpus, profile contract, CLI contract, and probe contract suites.
- Architecture contracts prove that core remains source-neutral, MCP types do not leak inward, serde-native wire handling stays in the Source Adapter layer, and every Atlassian request reuses the one shared HTTP substrate. No ACLI process or second HTTP dependency is permitted.
- Every new public method has happy-path and boundary/error coverage. Every typed sum variant, early return, status class, continuation terminal form, mutation-journal state, and required/optional health transition has a corresponding test. Missing and corrupt inputs remain distinct.
- Deterministic network tests use committed TLS roots and server-side request, body, accept, and flushed-byte observations. Every refusal/redaction/cancellation row has a positive control proving the fixture could have succeeded, preventing vacuous passes.
- Pagination tests cover empty, single-page, exact endpoint maximum, smaller returned maximum, 1,000-record limit, ten-request limit, terminal marker, missing/corrupt/foreign continuation, Link/body disagreement, spill to artifact, and separately exposed source continuation.
- Cache tests cover first fetch, conditional repeat, valid 304, changed ETag replacement, absent/oversized/unreadable validator, 304 without entry, generation invalidation, stale-repopulation prevention, query non-caching, product-local invalidation, and cache ceiling fallback without stale serving.
- Retry tests cover transport retry, delta-seconds, HTTP-date, bounded jitter, valid 429/503, missing/invalid/excessive timing, deadline refusal, non-retryable 5xx, cancellation during wait, POST-search idempotency, and the invariant that no mutation retries.
- Error/redaction tests cover every stable category, rate-signaled versus ordinary 403, hidden/absent objects, invalid query versus malformed reference, proven versus unproven conflict, structured validation bounds, trace-ID sanitation, malicious response prose, and canary secrets across errors, logs, reports, caches, artifacts, and stdio.
- Field round-trip tests prove canonical Jira JSON remains byte-stable after parse/re-encode, unknown ADF members survive, Confluence storage bytes remain exact, rendered unsupported markers stay deterministic, and unchanged authoritative Field content can be resubmitted without representation loss.
- Stateful mutation tests cover object serialization, stale preflight, external-race model, native Confluence version increments, companion-Field preservation, grants before egress, authoritative response/refetch, malformed success, Unknown outcomes, cache invalidation, operationId coalescing/replay/conflict/failure/Unknown, and canonical receipt validation.
- Release 1 adds exactly three ignored GET-only live rows gated by `RFS_LIVE=1` and reader credentials: Jira adapter, Confluence adapter, and full profile-to-stdio. They assert real shapes and invariants, forced cursor/Link pagination, stable identity/parentage, native representation/media, repeated-read identity, probe isolation, and redaction. They never assert tenant-wide counts, mutable timestamps, ETag presence, rate exhaustion, or perform mutation.
- A disposable tenant uses an administrator/provisioner only through an idempotent non-secret manifest-driven `curl`/`jq` bootstrap/verify/cleanup command. Live smokes receive only a least-privileged reader. Stable fixture IDs and profile references live in ignored local state; credentials are never written by the fixture command.
- OAuth is not declared supported until deterministic refresh/expiry/revocation/concurrency coverage and a recorded read-only live OAuth run pass.
- Release 3 and Release 4 require separately approved one-off write probes under both API-token and OAuth credentials. They record create/update responses, immediate authoritative refetch, permission/scope behavior, external-writer or stale-version behavior, returned identity/parent validation, post-write visibility, and provisioner cleanup. Permanent live tests remain read-only and never induce rate exhaustion.
- Every live or controlled probe is recorded in the owning implementation ticket's evidence artifact using the established premise, fixture, oracle, comparison, uncertainty, and run-result format.

## Out of Scope

- Jira or Confluence Data Center.
- ACLI integration, fallback, subprocess execution, or an ACLI abstraction seam.
- A second HTTP client, source-specific egress policy, dynamic Source Adapter plugins, or protocol types inside core.
- Cross-Site-Mount queries, fanout, merged Jira/Confluence query semantics, or a ResourceFS JQL/CQL parser.
- Attachment upload or download, Jira changelogs or worklogs, Confluence ancillary activity, or generic unsupported content Resources.
- Bulk issue, page, or comment creation or mutation.
- Jira workflow transitions, arbitrary incremental `update` operations, properties, history metadata, screen/workflow overrides, or ownership/status mutation.
- Deletion of Atlassian objects.
- Confluence hierarchy moves, space moves, owner transfer, draft/private/embedded/subtype creation, or historical-version mutation.
- Inline-comment resolution mutation.
- Mutation of Aggregates or aliases.
- Markdown-to-ADF conversion, Markdown-to-Confluence-storage conversion, rendered HTML as authority, or remote rendering/conversion fallback.
- Atlassian hashline editing, PUT/CUT patches, REM, or MV.
- Cross-session creation deduplication or any claim that ResourceFS operationId is transmitted upstream.
- A claim of atomic Jira compare-and-swap protection against external writers.
- Serving cached Atlassian content without upstream revalidation.
- Background health polling or circuit breakers.
- Automatic rate-limit exhaustion tests or permanent destructive live smokes.
- OAuth support in Release 1, mutation support before Release 3, or dormant public configuration/reference variants for later releases.

## Further Notes

- The closed Wayfinder map **Specify Atlassian Cloud Jira and Confluence Portable Sources** (`rfs-al1y`) and its linked decision tickets are the authoritative rationale and detail behind this consolidated specification.
- **Sequence the Atlassian read-first implementation milestones** defines the four release boundaries and evidence gates. The first release is independently useful and shippable; later releases must not delay or weaken its read-only contract.
- The latest Confluence research correction is authoritative: page-version listing with `body-format` is capped at 50, while the ordinary v2 maximum remains 250.
- Jira enhanced JQL is eventually consistent. ResourceFS preserves that fact and does not claim a query snapshot immediately after mutation.
- Jira issue/comment endpoints expose no documented atomic CAS validator. ResourceFS promises local object serialization and immediate compare-before-write only; external races remain possible and must be disclosed.
- The implementation should be split into dependency-linked tracer-bullet tickets after this spec. Tickets produced from this spec are already agent-ready and should not be triaged again.

title: Budget-sensitive tests flake on loaded CI runners
description:
Three tests fail intermittently on hosted CI runners without any related code change. All three were observed on PR #9 (rfs-0n97), where the same commit passed the push run and failed the pull_request run on the identical platform, which is what establishes them as flakes rather than regressions.

Observed failures:
1. crates/resourcefs-sources/tests/session_storage_contract.rs heartbeat_updates_persisted_liveness_within_budget - 'heartbeat took 505.275ms' against a 100 ms release budget, windows-latest.
2. crates/resourcefs-sources/tests/artifact_adapter_contract.rs glob_snapshot_excludes_its_recovery_artifact - 'C8 glob transient allocation exceeded 1 MiB: 2291599', reproduced locally on Linux as well as CI.
3. crates/resourcefs-mcp/tests/support/stdio.rs finish_process - 'resourcefs did not exit after stdin closed' at a 2 s deadline, windows-latest.

As an unblocking stopgap the budgets were raised (100 ms to 1000 ms; 1 MiB to 4 MiB; 2 s to 10 s). That is deliberately a symptom fix and this issue exists to do the real work.

The allocation one is not a budget problem at all. PEAK_ALLOCATED is a process-wide AtomicUsize fed by a #[global_allocator], and the tests in that binary run in parallel by default, so a concurrent test's allocations are attributed to the test under measurement. Raising the ceiling hides that; it does not correct it. The same pattern exists in filesystem_resource_limits_contract.rs and github_facts_contract.rs, so any fix should cover all three. Candidate approaches: serialise the measuring tests, scope the counter per-thread, or move allocation budgets into the separately gated ignored-budget inventory that already runs single-threaded.

The two timing budgets are host-dominated (a filesystem mtime write and a process teardown) and may simply belong in the ignored production-budget path rather than the functional suite, so that a shared runner's scheduling cannot fail the gate.

Worth noting alongside this: .github/workflows/ci.yml currently triggers on both push and pull_request with no branch filter, so every push to a branch with an open PR produces two runs that both write the same required 'gates (<os>)' status context. Whichever finishes last wins. On PR #9 the failing and passing windows-latest runs completed 15 seconds apart, so a flake can non-deterministically block a mergeable PR. rfs-k388-ci-gates already carries a fix for the duplicate runs, which reduces the exposure but does not remove the flakes.

title: Compare provider-selected merge base to head
description:
## What to build

Deliver merge-base comparison metadata and exact merge-base-to-head tree changes, plus separate provider-native comparison file/commit collections. Identify the provider-selected ancestor and expose native enumeration caps without substituting direct-tree semantics.

User stories covered: 11–17, 22, 28–38. Shared applicable safety/proof stories are included in every slice. Story 44 is the approved breakdown/publication process, not an implementation feature.

Source: GitHub Fact Resource contract specification in the sibling resourcefs-wt-github-resource-contract documentation worktree (docs/github-resource-contract-spec.md). User approved this eight-slice breakdown and dependency graph. Exact grammar/schema spellings marked PROPOSED remain subject to the specification's applicable design approval gate; issue creation does not waive that gate or authorize live tenant operations.

Shared contract (mandatory for every applicable path): existing public SourceAdapter/SourceResource; owned versioned /facts JSON, not private wire DTOs or Markdown scraping; unchanged human projections and five tools. ResourceFS owns acquisition; Cyril owns capture authorization/totals, retention, UI and review meaning. One configured deployment, explicit repository/fork/origin authority, embedder-supplied origin-bound credentials, new Path Session on principal change, REST 2022-11-28, validated selected ghe.com web/API pairing; no new sign-in flow or provider framework.

Preserve deployment/source identity, supplied native repository/object IDs and links, requested versus observed immutable operands, acquisition interval and REST version, supplied upstream versions/times separately, missing/null/unknown values and explicit coverage. VersionTag hashes representation bytes, not Git identity. Reuse the first slice's reviewed envelope and error vocabulary; additive optional fields permitted, unsupported major versions rejected. Keep one ResourceError with stable categories and bounded sanitized structured status/access ambiguity/retry/limit details; no message parsing, hidden-404-to-empty or denial-to-expired-login inference.

Per-read measurement targets: 10 physical attempts including parent lookups/revalidation/retries; 30 seconds shared across send/body/wait; 8 MiB per response; 16 MiB cumulative accepted response bodies; 16 MiB serialized JSON INCLUDING provenance/outcome/continuation; 4 MiB decoded regular-file bytes; 1,000 records per collection. Positive lower-only acquisition controls are separate from display limits: reject zero/above-hard-ceiling inputs and intersect valid requests with operator policy. These are not memory or wire-traffic guarantees. Measure implementation feasibility; do not silently raise ceilings. Reuse bounded retry/cache behavior and honor applicable rate guidance within the same deadline; failed revalidation cannot return stale success.

Collections admit whole verified pages only if all record/body/serialized budgets fit. Ordinary later failures preserve valid earlier pages with honest coverage, and continuation ONLY when valid; continuation is NOT required for retention. First failure without usable data is typed failure, not empty success. Cancellation or authority/requested-identity violations reject the current component including acquired pages. Continuations are credential-free, session-scoped and resource/operand/authority-bound; best-effort traversal, not snapshots. Expose provider caps separately; no invented recovery or exhaustive fallback to hide caps.

## Placement / boundaries

resourcefs-core extends slice 6 comparison modes/addresses. resourcefs-sources GitHub owns provider comparison validation and native file/commit projection, reusing exact tree changes and inherited bounded object/collection machinery. resourcefs-mcp uses existing integration. No local merge-base calculation, synthetic ancestor, generated native patches or alternate HTTP stack.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preserve requested base/head repository identities, observed operands, provider-selected merge-base SHA and actual left/right tree identities; exact tree changes do not come from capped native file rows.
- [ ] Diverged-history M-to-B omits the base-only reversal that A-to-B contains; compare both modes independently. Native comparison status is not a review verdict.
- [ ] Unavailable/contradictory valid merge base fails this mode explicitly, without local computation, uniqueness claim, synthetic base or automatic direct fallback. Unrelated history requires substantiation, not an access-hidden response; direct-tree stays independently usable.
- [ ] Native file/commit collections are separate Resources preserving native patches/status/paths with independent coverage. Compare files cap at 300 on the first page; later commit pages cannot recover files. Unpaginated 250-commit limit and paginated coverage remain distinct from local caps.
- [ ] Native cross-fork comparison respects provider-supported repository-network relationships and independent authority; unsupported/inaccessible relations never expand credentials or repositories.
- [ ] Each metadata/change/file/commit route uses public library, real MCP and applicable live proof under its own bounded read, with inherited partial/continuation and cancellation/integrity semantics.
- [ ] Complete this Resource path through validated addressing, configured Source Adapter acquisition/projection, catalog grammar/examples, applicable profile/CLI schema/check integration, public library consumption and real MCP read/recovery. No private inspector, new tool/provider trait or duplicate HTTP client.
- [ ] Independently observe expected upstream requests, requested/observed identities, zero forbidden egress and zero remote writes, including failure/retry/cancellation. Exercise applicable exact/over-limit controls, shared attempts/deadline, sanitized errors, partial retention and integrity overrides. Existing human reads retain their meaning.
- [ ] Library consumers parse complete bounded JSON; real MCP Recovery References reconstruct exactly acquired JSON before parsing. Source continuation is separately upstream acquisition under ADR-0006, not recovery of omitted output.
- [ ] Add applicable ignored live_* read-only smokes for new adapter and primary real rfs stdio paths, gated by RFS_LIVE=1 and GITHUB_TOKEN, skipping cleanly when absent. Record executed evidence and exact revision in the owning issue evidence record; use public/authorized controlled upstream shapes and invariants, not moving counts. Skipped rows are not passes.
- [ ] Run the repository-owned complete verification gate on the final implementation; record live proof separately. Actual numerical enforcement, deadline/transport and allocation behavior require implementation measurements, not inherited synthetic-probe claims. ResourceFS acceptance does not close Cyril corporate ghe.com/native Windows/credentials/storage/UI acceptance.

title: Relative PATH in command credentials passes rfs check but fails at serve time
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What is wrong

A credential command whose `environment.PATH` literal is a relative directory (for example `command-bin`) is validated by the static profile checker against the profile directory, but executed against the process working directory.

- `crates/resourcefs-mcp/src/profile/check.rs` `check_executable`: a relative `PATH` entry is joined onto `self.base` (the configuration base) before `is_executable_in`, so `rfs check` reports the helper as resolvable.
- `crates/resourcefs-sources/src/process/mod.rs` (`CommandExecutor::run`, ~line 586): the child is built with `env_clear()` + `envs(...)` and no `current_dir`, so the same relative entry resolves against wherever `rfs serve` was launched.

Observable failure: `rfs check` is green; `rfs serve --config /path/profile.json` from any other cwd fails the helper, `secret::resolve` returns `helper_failed`, the source becomes "source credential could not be resolved", and an optional source mounts visibly degraded while a required one fails startup — with no hint that the profile directory is the missing base.

History: the former `cli_contract::an_unmountable_kind_is_refused_before_it_is_probed` fence only passed because its process cwd *was* the profile directory. The replacement unit test `profile::check::tests::an_unmountable_kind_is_refused_before_its_credential_resolves` works around this by using an absolute `PATH`; drop that workaround once fixed.

## Fix shape

One of:
- Resolve relative `PATH` entries (and any relative `argv[0]` with a separator) to absolute paths under the configuration base at check time, so the executor receives what the checker validated; or
- Set `current_dir(configuration_base)` on the spawned child.

The first keeps the executor cwd-agnostic and is preferred; either way the checker and executor must agree.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A profile with a relative `PATH` literal in a command credential resolves the same helper under `rfs check` and `rfs serve` regardless of the process cwd.
- [ ] A unit or CLI fence launches from a cwd other than the profile directory and proves the helper ran (marker-file oracle).
- [ ] The absolute-`PATH` workaround in `an_unmountable_kind_is_refused_before_its_credential_resolves` is removed.

notes.content:
2026-08-27 fixed via the Gilfoyle change-workflow; routed Local and recorded at .rfs-7r1w/route.md (T1 no, T2 no, T3 no, T4 yes).

Cause: process/mod.rs::resolve_environment inserted a profile-declared PATH into the child environment verbatim while build_command never set current_dir, so the OS resolved relative entries against the launch directory; profile/check.rs::check_executable validates the same value by joining non-absolute entries onto the configuration base, which is cwd-independent. Reproduced at the product surface before the fix: identical `rfs check --probe --config <abs>` runs differed only by cwd — from the profile directory the helper ran, from the repo root it did not and the report carried "source credential could not be resolved", while plain `rfs check` was green from both.

Fix: resolve_environment now takes the command base and rewrites a declared PATH through resolve_declared_path, joining every non-absolute entry (including the POSIX empty entry) onto the already-canonicalized base. This extends the rule resolve_program has always applied to a relative argv[0], so one rule governs every relative path a command spec names, and the child's working directory is left untouched. An undeclared PATH is still inherited from the operator's ambient environment unchanged; the resulting narrow divergence from the checker for an ambient PATH carrying a relative entry is recorded in route.md rather than left implicit.

Fences (each verified to FAIL under the named mutation "forward a declared PATH verbatim", then pass): process_contract::declared_relative_path_resolves_against_the_command_base (child reports the PATH it was handed), process_contract::declared_relative_path_resolves_a_bare_program (unix; a bare argv[0] actually resolves through it), and profile::check::tests::an_unmountable_kind_is_refused_before_its_credential_resolves, whose absolute-PATH workaround is now removed per the third acceptance criterion — it uses a relative PATH and never chdirs, so its positive control fences this bug.

Verification: workspace suite 59/59, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, scripts/live-smoke.sh all three rows green. Post-fix reproduction: run D now runs the helper with no credential diagnostic; controls C and E unchanged.

Closed: Fixed: a profile-declared relative PATH now resolves against the configuration base in resolve_environment, matching check_executable and the existing resolve_program rule. All three acceptance criteria met; fences verified against a named mutation; product-surface repro confirmed fixed.

2026-08-27 follow-up on requester decision: exact checker/executor parity. The first fix rewrote only a profile-declared PATH and deliberately forwarded the ambient inherited PATH unchanged, which left one narrow divergence — check_executable joins non-absolute entries onto the base for its ambient fallback too (`if path.is_none() { path = self.environment_value("PATH") }`), so for an ambient PATH carrying a relative entry the checker stayed stricter than the executor. The requester chose parity, so the rewrite now applies to whichever PATH the child ends up with, declared or inherited, in one post-pass over the resolved environment (resolve_declared_path renamed resolve_search_path). An ambient PATH holding only absolute entries — the normal case — is unchanged.

Routing: the scope decision reran all four tests. T1/T2/T3 keep their verdicts and evidence (same mechanism and premises, same private function, one more bounded rewrite of an in-memory string); T4 keeps `yes` with behavior point (4) rewritten. Route remains Local; .rfs-7r1w/route.md carries the revision, the rewritten contract, and a second recorded result.

New fence: process_contract::inherited_relative_path_resolves_against_the_command_base, which controls the ambient PATH by re-executing the test in a child process rather than by set_var (which would race the other tests in the binary). Two named mutations were checked: "forward PATH verbatim" fails all four fences, and "exempt the inherited PATH" — the superseded behavior — fails only the new one, so the fence discriminates this revision specifically rather than the fix as a whole.

Verification: process_contract 8/8, workspace 59/59, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, scripts/live-smoke.sh all three rows green, and the product-surface repro still runs the helper from a cwd that is not the profile directory.
