## Implementation Decisions

### Product and interface

- ResourceFS is an independent Rust product, repository, package, and release. OMP is design input, not a runtime dependency or continuing compatibility authority.
- The official Rust `rmcp` SDK provides the local stdio MCP runtime. ResourceFS advertises MCP `2026-07-28`, negotiates supported revisions, and feature-gates optional capabilities.
- Product SemVer is the Behavior Contract version. Breaking reference grammar, tool schema, result, or mutation semantics require a major release. Profile and import formats use separate integer schema versions.
- The canonical model-controlled interface is exactly five `rfs_*` tools: read, search, glob, write, and edit.
- All tools remain discoverable. Read-only/destructive annotations are advisory; the policy engine authorizes each operation against its resolved destination.
- `rfs_read`, `rfs_search`, and `rfs_glob` accept lower-only per-call limits. Selectors choose content projections; limit fields only constrain output.
- `rfs_write` accepts path, UTF-8 content, conditional Version Tag, and operation ID metadata. Replacements require the current Version Tag. Remote Creation Targets require an operation ID.
- `rfs_edit` accepts the versioned hashline patch language with line-anchored `PUT`, `CUT`, `REM`, and same-source `MV`.
- Every tool returns complete non-empty TextContent and a structured object. Every output schema has an object root.
- Tool errors expose stable semantic categories. MCP protocol/schema errors remain protocol errors.
- MCP Resources and templates mirror the same address space when negotiated. Tools remain canonical because client Resource support is inconsistent.
- Resource listing is bounded and paginated. Completion is local/fast. Only workspace/local and Path Session Resources publish subscription changes initially.
- No MCP Prompts or Tasks are exposed in 1.0. Essential instructions live early in tool descriptions and in initialization instructions.

### Reference and Resource contract

- A Path Reference contains a source namespace, Resource identity/hierarchy, and optional projection selector. The operation is never encoded as a new tool family.
- Existing literal filesystem paths take precedence over selector interpretation. Windows drives and UNC paths remain filesystem paths.
- Literal ambiguous delimiters are percent-encoded. Rendered references use canonical slash form.
- Relative paths resolve only under the Primary Workspace Root. Any declared root is directly addressable through canonical `rfs://workspace/<root>/<path>` input.
- Workspace MCP Resource identity remains private `rfs://` by default. Optional backing-path visibility adds `file://` metadata without changing canonical identity.
- Internal schemes are server-relative. ResourceFS preserves OMP-compatible spellings where portable but makes no global URI ownership claim.
- Included families are workspace files/directories, ZIP/tar archives, SQLite, HTTPS, converted documents, images, notebooks, session artifacts/scratch, memory, skills, rules, vaults, GitHub issues/PRs, SSH, Agent Exports, and downstream MCP Resources.
- OMP-runtime schemes for OMP docs, security findings, and tool devices are excluded.
- Downstream MCP proxies Resources/templates only, over direct-argv stdio or allowlisted Streamable HTTP. It never proxies tools or prompts.
- Known duplicate downstream native URIs fail configuration. Ambiguous template expansions fail at resolution.

### Projections and Source Adapters

- Parseable code defaults to Structural Summary. The compiled registry covers Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, C/C++, and C#. Unsupported or oversized inputs use bounded text fallback.
- Structural Summaries expose declarations, elide bodies, and name exact recovery selectors.
- Archive adapters enforce member containment and rebuild mutable archives through atomic replacement.
- SQLite rows are JSON Resources addressed by scalar or canonical composite keys. Writes insert or fully replace, edits operate on JSON projections, deletes use `REM`, and all mutations are transactional. Arbitrary mutating SQL is excluded.
- HTTPS defaults to reader-mode Markdown/text; `:raw` returns the bounded original body. Every redirect and resolved address is reauthorized.
- Document conversion is configured by direct argv and remains a read projection.
- Image reads return typed image content plus complete textual metadata. Unsupported arbitrary binary data is metadata/blob-readable but not mutable.
- Notebook reads use deterministic cell markers. Versioned edits preserve notebook metadata and retained cell metadata/outputs, support cell insertion/reorder/deletion, and reject malformed projections.
- GitHub aggregates are read-only. Title, body, and conversation comments are Field Resources.
- GitHub issue creation uses strict title frontmatter plus Markdown body. PR creation requires title/head/base, permits draft, and uses Markdown body.
- GitHub post-creation mutation is limited to title, body, and conversation comments. Labels, assignees, status, reviews, and inline review comments are read-only in 1.0.
- Operation IDs deduplicate only within one live Path Session. Reuse with different content fails. Unknown upstream outcomes are never automatically retried; callers reconcile before repeating after disconnect.
- SSH is read-only, uses system SSH/host-key verification, and permits only configured host aliases.
- Skills follow the Agent Skills format. Native rules use a strict versioned manifest mapping name, description, glob scope, and contained Markdown.
- Memory is a read-only configured file/directory projection.
- Vault Resources understand Obsidian notes, wikilinks, properties, tasks, and bases; grant-controlled text mutations preserve unrelated frontmatter.
- Agent/history imports use a public strict versioned manifest and contained files; they never inspect private harness layouts and remain read-only.
- `/home/dwalleck/.omp/agent/sessions/-repos-oh-my-pi/2026-08-18T02-52-52-195Z_01a012c9-3863-7000-a568-fa76cdae77fc/local` is caller-authored Session Scratch. `artifact://` is immutable server-authored recovery storage.

### Mutation, authority, and concurrency

- Workspace Roots and mutable Portable Sources declare independent create, update, and delete grants. Merely configuring an adapter grants no mutation.
- Version Tags derive from authoritative content rather than timestamps.
- Read snapshots bind Version Tags to the displayed projection/regions, preventing edits to guessed unseen content.
- Existing-resource writes require `ifVersion`; hashline edits carry the read header and Version Tag.
- Mutation validates current authoritative state immediately before commit and serializes per canonical Resource.
- Filesystem and archive mutation uses atomic replacement, SQLite uses transactions, and remote adapters use the strongest available compare-before-write behavior without claiming unavailable upstream atomicity.
- `REM` is the sole deletion syntax. `MV` is same-source only and requires delete/create authority. Cross-source moves and binary writes fail.
- Failed validation does not change authoritative state.

### Sessions, roots, configuration, and security

- One MCP connection owns one Path Session: artifacts, scratch, snapshots, caches, operation journal, and source handles.
- Disconnect invalidates Path Session references immediately. Cache files remain only until configured TTL cleanup.
- Non-empty client MCP Roots take precedence. Otherwise exactly one launch source supplies roots: one Server Profile or CLI roots, never both.
- Multiple roots require a uniquely matching primary-root selector before relative references work.
- Client root changes immediately re-derive authority, invalidate removed-root snapshots/references, and retain session-owned scratch/artifacts.
- At most one strict JSON Server Profile is loaded. Unknown fields, invalid policy, unsafe paths, and registration conflicts fail startup.
- Profiles configure sources, required/degraded behavior, mutation grants, repository/host/path allowlists, private-network grants, lower limits, session cache/TTL, backing-path visibility, secret references, converters, and downstream MCP definitions.
- Secrets are references, never inline values. Helper commands run without a shell, with hard time/output caps and only a minimal explicit environment.
- Required unavailable sources fail startup. Optional unavailable sources enter visible Degraded Source state and fail only their own references.
- HTTPS is host-allowlisted. Loopback, link-local, private, and special addresses require separate explicit grants and are revalidated across redirects/resolution.
- Canonical path containment follows real targets, including symlinks/reparse points. Archive paths receive equivalent containment checks.
- Logging never uses protocol stdout, redacts credentials, and emits no telemetry.
- The CLI exposes serve, check, and schema operations only. Configuration checking has an explicit non-mutating external probe mode.

### Limits, architecture, and distribution

- Built-in hard ceilings are 48 KiB/3,000 lines/512 columns for text results, 5 MiB per embedded image, 64 MiB per artifact or scratch object, 256 MiB per Path Session, and 1,000 entries per listing page.
- Profiles and calls may lower but never raise the binary’s hard ceilings.
- Omitted successful output spills losslessly to immutable Recovery References. A spill that would exceed quota fails with a bounded limit error. Live references are never evicted.
- The Rust workspace contains three principal deep modules: the core engine, compiled Source Adapters, and the MCP/CLI adapter.
- The core engine owns reference parsing, selectors, Resource/result/error types, policy, Path Sessions, snapshots/tags, limits, recovery, and mutation coordination.
- The sources module contains all compiled adapters. Configuration creates adapter instances; dynamic plugins are not supported.
- The MCP module owns protocol negotiation, schemas, content rendering, cancellation, Resources/templates/completion/subscriptions, Kiro compatibility, and CLI composition.
- A shared Source Adapter interface covers resolution, projection, versioning, enumeration, mutation, and source capability/policy behavior.
- GitHub uses native HTTP. SSH uses system SSH. Archives support ZIP/tar families. Structural parsing uses a curated tree-sitter registry. Search uses Rust regex plus PCRE2.
- Prebuilt Linux/macOS/Windows releases and `cargo install` are first-class distribution contracts.

## Testing Decisions

- The highest behavioral seam is the compiled `resourcefs` process over stdio MCP. End-to-end contract tests launch the real binary with temporary Workspace Roots and deterministic local/fake upstreams, then call the five tools and mirrored Resources exactly as a harness does.
- The user explicitly requires every Source Adapter to be tested directly in addition to the MCP seam. Direct adapter suites verify each source’s resolution, projection, versioning, enumeration, mutation, containment, and error mapping. Global behavior such as MCP rendering and Kiro fallbacks stays at the external seam rather than being duplicated in every adapter suite.
- A good test asserts externally observable behavior: returned text/structured content, canonical Path References, Version Tags, authoritative state changes, stable error categories, recovery, permissions, and boundedness. Tests do not assert private field assignment, helper call order, crate internals, or source text.
- The core engine receives focused contract and property tests for reference parsing, selector algebra, Version Tags, snapshot visibility, policy decisions, quota accounting, per-Resource mutation serialization, and Path Session/root transitions.
- Filesystem adapter tests cover relative/absolute/root-qualified references, multi-root primary selection, symlinks/reparse points, literal-selector precedence, Windows forms, atomic write failure, stale versions, `REM`, and same-source `MV`.
- Archive adapter tests cover ZIP/tar families, traversing/absolute member rejection, member reads/search/glob, create/replace/edit/delete/move, metadata preservation where promised, and atomic rebuild failure.
- SQLite adapter tests cover scalar/composite keys, canonical encoding, row JSON transformation, key mismatch, insert/replace/edit/delete, constraints, transactions, concurrency, invalid schema, and read-only queries.
- Document/image/notebook adapter tests cover converter failure/timeout/output caps, image metadata and payload ceilings, unsupported binary behavior, deterministic notebook projections, marker escaping, metadata/output preservation, type changes, insertion/reorder/deletion, invalid JSON, and malformed edits.
- HTTPS adapter tests use controlled servers to cover reader mode, raw mode, MIME/encoding, redirects, DNS/address revalidation, host/private-network policy, body limits, cancellation, and credential redaction.
- GitHub adapter tests use a deterministic fake HTTP upstream to cover repository allowlists, aggregate/Field Resource separation, title/body/comment mutation, issue/PR creation documents, conversation versus review comments, compare-before-write behavior, operation-ID reuse, unknown outcomes, and policy denial.
- SSH adapter tests use a controlled SSH fixture or argv-level executable fixture to cover host allowlists, normal host-key failure propagation, UTF-8/output caps, cancellation, minimal environment, and mutation rejection.
- Skill/rule/memory/vault tests cover manifest/schema validation, containment, symlink escape, Agent Skills resolution, rule glob metadata, read-only memory, vault wikilinks/properties/tasks/bases, frontmatter preservation, and grant-controlled mutations.
- Agent Export tests cover schema versions, parent/child relationships, stable IDs, contained paths, missing output/transcript files, malicious traversal, read-only behavior, and bounded listing.
- Downstream MCP adapter tests launch deterministic stdio and HTTP resource servers to cover negotiation, listing, templates, completion, native URI preservation, global collisions, ambiguous expansions, degraded/required sources, binary/text contents, limits, cancellation, and the absence of tool/prompt proxying.
- Session-resource adapter tests cover scratch create/replace/edit/delete/move, artifact immutability, object/session quotas, no live eviction, disconnect invalidation, TTL cleanup, operation journals, and cross-session isolation.
- Official MCP conformance suites verify supported negotiated server revisions. Output-schema regression fixtures require object roots and non-empty text fallbacks.
- The real Kiro CLI is a release acceptance seam. Protected CI runs startup, discovery, read, spill/recovery, search, scratch write/read, and permission denial with a secret; a recorded interactive run is the fallback where headless credentials are unavailable.
- Cross-platform binary smoke tests run on Linux, macOS, and Windows. They exercise path parsing, installation, process startup, stdio cleanliness, and one representative read/write/recovery scenario.
- Parser fuzzing targets Path Reference parsing, selector parsing, hashline patches, archive member names, percent encoding, composite SQLite keys, manifests, and strict profile schemas. Fuzzing supplements but does not replace behavioral assertions.
- Stress fixtures cover large files, deep directories, many search matches, maximum listings, large images, artifact/session exhaustion, concurrent operations, slow/cancelled sources, and parser fallback without unbounded memory growth.
- Prior art comes from OMP’s observable read-selector, internal-resource routing, hashline edit, notebook round-trip, output-spill, and MCP lifecycle behavior. ResourceFS copies useful fixture ideas into its own Behavior Contract rather than importing OMP implementation or asserting permanent parity.

## Out of Scope

- OMP runtime integration, OMP configuration discovery, private OMP session-layout inspection, or continuing OMP conformance.
- Remote or multi-tenant ResourceFS transport; 1.0 is a local stdio server.
- OMP-owned documentation, security-scan, or virtual tool-device schemes.
- Dynamic Source Adapter plugins.
- MCP Prompt or Task surfaces.
- Downstream MCP tool or prompt proxying.
- Arbitrary mutating SQL.
- Arbitrary binary mutation.
- Cross-source moves.
- SSH mutation.
- Mutable Memory Resources or imported agent/history data.
- GitHub labels, assignees, status, reviews, or inline-review mutation after object creation.
- Automatic retries after unknown remote creation outcomes.
- Cross-session operation-ID deduplication.
- Interactive profile management or a configuration UI.
- Telemetry.

## Further Notes

- The accepted domain glossary and ADRs are normative. Use the canonical terms Path Reference, Resource, Workspace Root, Portable Source, Path Session, Server Profile, Recovery Reference, Session Scratch, Workspace Mutation, Source Mutation, Mutation Policy, Structural Summary, Behavior Contract, Version Tag, Aggregate Resource, Field Resource, Creation Target, Agent Export, Resource Mirror, Degraded Source, Source Adapter, and Backing-Path Visibility.
- Kiro CLI is the compatibility floor, not the only intended client. Its current limitations require complete text fallbacks, object-root output schemas, inline Recovery References, and conservative output bounds.
- The official Rust MCP SDK was selected because it provides the required stdio server/client, tool, Resource/template, structured-content, cancellation, and conformance support. Experimental MCP Tasks are unnecessary.
- This issue specifies the complete 1.0 product. Subsequent ticket decomposition should preserve the accepted interfaces and split implementation by independently verifiable Behavior Contract slices rather than by crate scaffolding alone.

title: Define transactional database mutation and concurrency semantics
description:
## Question

What provider-neutral contract makes insert, full replace, hashline edit, and delete safe across SQLite and SQL Server? Resolve path/body key agreement, generated fields, transaction boundaries, immediate compare-before-commit, content-derived tags versus SQL Server `rowversion`, no-rowversion comparison, exactly-one-row effects, external-writer races, per-Resource locking, seen-region snapshots for `db://` rows, cancellation after commit begins, rollback/error mapping, and which operations may be unsupported per table.

notes.content:
Requester-approved resolution.

Identity and inputs: known-key insert targets the canonical row Resource. Generated-key insert revises the earlier hierarchy clause by adding `db://<mount>/<schema>/<table>/new` as a typed Creation Target, not a row Resource or writable table aggregate; it requires `operationId` and returns the generated canonical row identity. Canonical JSON key segments keep ordinary row keys distinct from the reserved target. Mixed generated composite keys supply every caller-controlled PK member and omit generated members; generated creation is unsupported unless the provider can recover the complete key. Known-key bodies include the complete PK and agree Database-Value-for-Database-Value with the path. Keys are immutable. Insert requires every writable non-defaulted field, lets omission invoke only declared defaults/generated values, preserves explicit null as SQL NULL, and rejects supplied generated/read-only fields. Full replace requires every writable field; generated/read-only fields may be omitted or echoed exactly but never assigned. Edit follows the same read-only/key rules.

Transaction and concurrency: each row mutation holds the process-local per-canonical-Resource lock across one short explicit transaction on one connection. The lock serializes Path Sessions in this process only; external processes/writers are controlled by database transaction and conditional-DML authority. SQL Server uses READ COMMITTED plus atomic conditional DML. SQLite uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE before authoritative load/compare. Transaction-time catalog validation, authoritative state load, expected-state comparison, exactly one target DML, generated/trigger-complete reread, canonicalization and content-derived tag calculation, and COMMIT are one unit. Any conclusive pre-commit failure rolls back and publishes no state or receipt. Rollback failure makes the outcome unknown. A semantic no-op across every writable Database Value skips DML, preserving rowversion and avoiding triggers.

The public Version Tag remains SHA-256 over the complete authoritative canonical row; SQL Server rowversion never replaces it. SQL Server conditional DML uses PK plus the exact old rowversion when present. Without rowversion, and for SQLite, comparison uses the PK plus the complete visible original Database Value snapshot with null-safe equality or an observably equivalent comparison under the held SQLite writer transaction. If any authoritative changeable value cannot be projected and compared losslessly, mutation is unsupported for that table. Transaction-time schema drift that changes a still-supported canonical row invalidates the expected tag as version_conflict; current schema that cannot satisfy projection or the verb returns unsupported_projection or unsupported_mutation. Cached schema is never commit authority.

Effects: create against an existing key, replace/delete against a missing or stale expected row, PK/UNIQUE collision, and zero-row conditional DML are version_conflict. Exactly one addressed target effect succeeds. More than one target effect is an adapter/schema invariant breach: roll back and return source_unavailable. Standalone absent reads remain not_found. Triggers and referential actions are allowed database authority inside the same transaction; ResourceFS counts the addressed target DML independently of trigger rowcounts/NOCOUNT, rereads after trigger execution, permits delete cascades, and marks the operation unsupported when it cannot recover an unambiguous target identity/post-state.

Hashline edit: extend core Path Session snapshot identity to canonical editable Source Resources, including `db://` rows, rather than introducing adapter-owned snapshots. A row read records displayed regions against the whole-row authoritative tag. Edit applies only to previously displayed canonical JSON lines, then validates semantic JSON, keys, types, and read-only fields through the adapter. The adapter returns canonical post-state. Because normalization and generated/computed values can change positions/content, success invalidates the old snapshot and does not synthesize coverage for the new tag; another edit requires a fresh read.

Receipts and cancellation: successful insert/replace/edit receipts contain the canonical row reference and authoritative post-write Version Tag; generated-key operation-journal success stores both for replay. Delete returns the former canonical reference without a tag. Cancellation wins only before commit ownership. After commit ownership, cancellation is masked and the operation awaits a definitive outcome. Lost commit acknowledgement, failed rollback, or otherwise uncertain durability returns source_unavailable with explicit unknown-outcome/reconciliation guidance, retires the connection, and is never automatically retried. `/new` uses the existing exact-input Path-Session `operationId` journal, which blocks repeats after an unknown result; other unknown mutations require caller read/reconciliation before another attempt.

Capabilities and errors: table metadata advertises known-key create, generated-key create, replace, edit, and delete independently, each with a stable unsupported reason; every verb fails closed when its guarantees cannot be met. Add Behavior Contract category `invalid_content`. It covers malformed row JSON, duplicate/unknown/missing properties, Database Value/type errors, path/body mismatch, read-only assignment, and NOT NULL/CHECK/FK/type/length failures. `invalid_patch` remains patch syntax/unseen-coordinate failure. `version_conflict` covers the optimistic and uniqueness cases above; `permission_denied` covers database authorization; `unsupported_mutation` covers table/verb incapability; `unsupported_projection` covers unreadable schema/value projection; `limit_exceeded` covers bounds; `cancelled` is pre-commit cancellation only; and `source_unavailable` covers transport/timeouts/deadlocks/busy exhaustion, rollback failure, unknown commit, or adapter invariant breach. Provider-native details remain in messages/evidence, not categories.

No new decision ticket is required. “Reconcile SQLite with generic Database Mounts” consumes the SQLite transaction/capability consequences, and “Draft and approve the Database Mount specification and ADR” owns the coherent repository specification, Behavior Contract category update, core authoritative-edit/receipt seam, examples, and acceptance/live-smoke gates.
Closed: Requester approved the provider-neutral database mutation, transaction, concurrency, edit-snapshot, capability, receipt, cancellation, and error contract.

title: Read immutable commit and exact source Fact Resources
description:
## What to build

Deliver github:// immutable commit metadata and commit/path source facts. Expose exact regular-file bytes in base64, Git object/mode identity and explicit oversized/unsupported outcomes without lossy decoding or implicit target traversal.

User stories covered: 9–11, 17–21, 38–42. Shared applicable safety/proof stories are included in every slice. Story 44 is the approved breakdown/publication process, not an implementation feature.

Source: GitHub Fact Resource contract specification in the sibling resourcefs-wt-github-resource-contract documentation worktree (docs/github-resource-contract-spec.md). User approved this eight-slice breakdown and dependency graph. Exact grammar/schema spellings marked PROPOSED remain subject to the specification's applicable design approval gate; issue creation does not waive that gate or authorize live tenant operations.

Shared contract (mandatory for every applicable path): existing public SourceAdapter/SourceResource; owned versioned /facts JSON, not private wire DTOs or Markdown scraping; unchanged human projections and five tools. ResourceFS owns acquisition; Cyril owns capture authorization/totals, retention, UI and review meaning. One configured deployment, explicit repository/fork/origin authority, embedder-supplied origin-bound credentials, new Path Session on principal change, REST 2022-11-28, validated selected ghe.com web/API pairing; no new sign-in flow or provider framework.

Preserve deployment/source identity, supplied native repository/object IDs and links, requested versus observed immutable operands, acquisition interval and REST version, supplied upstream versions/times separately, missing/null/unknown values and explicit coverage. VersionTag hashes representation bytes, not Git identity. Reuse the first slice's reviewed envelope and error vocabulary; additive optional fields permitted, unsupported major versions rejected. Keep one ResourceError with stable categories and bounded sanitized structured status/access ambiguity/retry/limit details; no message parsing, hidden-404-to-empty or denial-to-expired-login inference.

Per-read measurement targets: 10 physical attempts including parent lookups/revalidation/retries; 30 seconds shared across send/body/wait; 8 MiB per response; 16 MiB cumulative accepted response bodies; 16 MiB serialized JSON INCLUDING provenance/outcome/continuation; 4 MiB decoded regular-file bytes; 1,000 records per collection. Positive lower-only acquisition controls are separate from display limits: reject zero/above-hard-ceiling inputs and intersect valid requests with operator policy. These are not memory or wire-traffic guarantees. Measure implementation feasibility; do not silently raise ceilings. Reuse bounded retry/cache behavior and honor applicable rate guidance within the same deadline; failed revalidation cannot return stale success.

Collections admit whole verified pages only if all record/body/serialized budgets fit. Ordinary later failures preserve valid earlier pages with honest coverage, and continuation ONLY when valid; continuation is NOT required for retention. First failure without usable data is typed failure, not empty success. Cancellation or authority/requested-identity violations reject the current component including acquired pages. Continuations are credential-free, session-scoped and resource/operand/authority-bound; best-effort traversal, not snapshots. Expose provider caps separately; no invented recovery or exhaustive fallback to hide caps.

## Placement / boundaries

resourcefs-core owns validated repository/commit/path addressing and canonical identity. resourcefs-sources GitHub owns pinned commit/tree/blob acquisition and byte-preserving projection through the existing HTTP substrate. resourcefs-mcp owns catalog/profile/read integration. Reuse slice 1 schema/errors/controls; no Git-specific object logic in core, binary transport redesign, clone or Cyril content client.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Commit facts retain immutable SHA/tree/parent SHAs and links, message, native author/committer identities/times and supplied GitHub accounts. No branch-tip or synthetic-merge substitution.
- [ ] Validate commit/tree/path/mode/blob relationships. Binary/non-UTF-8/newline-sensitive regular bytes round-trip exactly through base64. Enforce decoded 4 MiB independently: 4 MiB and 4 MiB+1 have equal encoded length in the probe; over-limit exposes verified identity/size with no accepted partial-file bytes or invented recovery.
- [ ] Executable modes, symlinks, submodule target identity and committed LFS pointers preserve Git meaning without following links/submodules or hydrating LFS. Object acquisition itself is bounded.
- [ ] Canonical escaping round-trips representable Unicode nested paths, percent/colon/question/hash, spaces and a filename facts; decode once. Reject malformed escapes/traversal aliases/encoded separators and provider-unrepresentable paths rather than change identity or silently omit coverage.
- [ ] Fork/source repositories require explicit authorization. Inaccessible/deleted fork or unknown object cannot trigger another repository fetch or moving-ref substitution. No chunked blob acquisition is added.
- [ ] Complete this Resource path through validated addressing, configured Source Adapter acquisition/projection, catalog grammar/examples, applicable profile/CLI schema/check integration, public library consumption and real MCP read/recovery. No private inspector, new tool/provider trait or duplicate HTTP client.
- [ ] Independently observe expected upstream requests, requested/observed identities, zero forbidden egress and zero remote writes, including failure/retry/cancellation. Exercise applicable exact/over-limit controls, shared attempts/deadline, sanitized errors, partial retention and integrity overrides. Existing human reads retain their meaning.
- [ ] Library consumers parse complete bounded JSON; real MCP Recovery References reconstruct exactly acquired JSON before parsing. Source continuation is separately upstream acquisition under ADR-0006, not recovery of omitted output.
- [ ] Add applicable ignored live_* read-only smokes for new adapter and primary real rfs stdio paths, gated by RFS_LIVE=1 and GITHUB_TOKEN, skipping cleanly when absent. Record executed evidence and exact revision in the owning issue evidence record; use public/authorized controlled upstream shapes and invariants, not moving counts. Skipped rows are not passes.
- [ ] Run the repository-owned complete verification gate on the final implementation; record live proof separately. Actual numerical enforcement, deadline/transport and allocation behavior require implementation measurements, not inherited synthetic-probe claims. ResourceFS acceptance does not close Cyril corporate ghe.com/native Windows/credentials/storage/UI acceptance.

title: Carry a typed source continuation alongside artifact recovery on overflowing reads and searches
description:
## Parent

rfs-jk0d — Build ResourceFS 1.0 as a standalone path-shaped MCP server

## What to build

A read or search result has one `continuationReference`. When a source projection both (a) overflows the inline page and (b) names a further upstream page (a GitHub collection `:page:<n>` continuation), the artifact continuation must win — it is the only route to the bytes cut from the page — so the typed source continuation survives only as text: the adapter's trailing `Continuation: …` line inside the retained artifact, or the `!<ref>\tcontinuation\t…` trailer row the Discovery Engine appends to a retained search document. A client only reaches `:page:11` by paging to the end of the artifact chain and reading it.

The structural fix is a second slot on the read and search results (for example `sourceContinuation`, or a small ordered list of continuations with their kind) rendered alongside `continuationReference`, so the upstream page is addressable from the first response. This is an MCP result-schema change (`schema_contract`, `stdio_mcp_contract`, `render.rs`) and touches the same surface rfs-ww6w must decide when it mirrors collections as cursor-paginated MCP Resources — decide it there, or at least consistently with it.

Context: `SourceResource::with_continuation` (core `resource.rs`), `ReadEngine::read` unbounded-branch handling (core `read.rs`), `DiscoveryEngine::retain_omitted` trailer (core `discovery.rs`), and the fences `read_engine_contract::source_continuations_surface_unless_the_page_itself_overflows` and `discovery_engine_contract::source_continuations_survive_artifact_recovery`, all landed with the rfs-45ww review fixes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A read of a >1,000-object GitHub collection that overflows 48 KiB exposes `issue://o/r:page:11` structurally in its first response, not only as text at the end of the artifact chain.
- [ ] A search whose records overflow the page exposes the source continuation structurally alongside the artifact continuation.
- [ ] The MCP schema and stdio contracts cover the new field; the text trailers remain as the artifact-level fallback.
- [ ] The decision is recorded consistently with rfs-ww6w's Resource pagination design.

notes.content: 2026-08-27 implemented (ADR-0006, docs/adr/0006-source-continuation-alongside-recovery.md). Decision: a second optional field, sourceContinuationReference, on rfs_read and rfs_search results (not rfs_glob), present only when continuationReference walks an artifact chain that would otherwise hide the typed upstream page; when the page fits, continuationReference already names the source's next page and the field is absent, so every prior result is byte-identical. Client rule: follow continuationReference until absent, then follow the sourceContinuationReference you were given. Behavior Contract 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 (additive). Core: ReadResource / SearchResult gain source_continuation_reference; ReadEngine and DiscoveryEngine set it on overflow; the text trailers stay as the artifact-level fallback. MCP: ReadToolOutput / SearchToolOutput field + "Source Continuation Reference:" text line; tool descriptions; output-schema fence in stdio_mcp_contract. Fences: render unit test (fits vs overflow for read and search), read_engine_contract and discovery_engine_contract rows. Live proof: stdio_live_smoke S3 against rust-lang/rust returned continuationReference artifact://...:page:49152 together with sourceContinuationReference issue://rust-lang/rust:page:11. Rejected: a list of continuations (one collection has one next page; aggregates name sub-collection continuations in text). rfs-ww6w should expose collection pagination through the same typed continuations.
Closed: Implemented as ADR-0006: sourceContinuationReference on read/search results, Behavior Contract 1.1.0; proven live (stdio_live_smoke S3) and fenced in core, render, and stdio schema contracts.

title: Flaky GitHub facts in-flight deadline test
description:
## What is wrong

`facts_inflight_cancel_and_deadline_refuse_barrier_delayed_response` in `crates/resourcefs-sources/tests/github_facts_contract.rs` fails intermittently. The `cancel = false` leg arms a 100 ms deadline and expects the read to fail with `source_unavailable` / `deadline_exceeded` before the fixture releases the blocked response. Under load the read occasionally succeeds instead, and the test panics at the `expect_err("late response cannot publish")` / bounded-response assertions.

Observed on the base branch `feat/rfs-0n97` (084d136) as well as on `feat/rfs-bfwa`, so it is not specific to the conversation-comment slice. Roughly 1 in 4 full-suite runs and 2 in 6 single-test runs failed on an otherwise idle workstation.

## Why it matters

The complete repository gate (`python scripts/ci-gates.py`) runs this suite; an intermittent failure makes a green gate non-reproducible and can mask real regressions in the deadline path.

## Suggested direction

Either make the barrier deterministic (e.g. drive the deadline with tokio time pause/advance rather than a wall-clock 100 ms) or widen the timing margin while keeping the deadline refusal assertion.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed upstream at the seam by 4a25e71 on PR #9: the fixture router now runs off the runtime worker, so the blocking barrier no longer parks a worker and the 100 ms deadline is serviced. This branch's superseded workaround was reverted on rebase and the test's original timing assertion stands.

title: Specify provider-neutral Database Mounts
description:
## Destination

Produce an approved, decision-complete implementation specification plus a focused ADR for provider-neutral `db://` Database Mounts with compiled SQLite and conventional SQL Server providers. The specification covers the full discovery/read/search/insert/replace/hashline-edit/delete contract while permitting read-only-first delivery.

## Notes

- Domain: ResourceFS Path References, Portable Sources, Source Adapters, Mutation Policy, Version Tags, Path Sessions, and the settled Database Mount and Database Value terms in `CONTEXT.md`.
- Starting evidence: `docs/research/sql-server-path-resources.md`.
- Every session consults `domain-modeling`; HITL decision tickets use `grilling`; transport evidence uses `research` then `prototype`; Rust prototype work also consults `rust-best-practices` and `codebase-design`.
- Canonical product term: **Database Mount** — a configured Portable Source instance binding one Server Profile-unique lowercase Mount ID to one provider and one logical database for the process/profile lifetime.
- Canonical value term: **Database Value** — a lossless native JSON scalar or recognized tagged extension used consistently in canonical row content and primary-key identity.
- Standing scope choices: generic `db://<mount>/...` namespace; one mount = one database; compiled provider registry; SQLite and conventional SQL Server providers; full contract with phased delivery.
- Validated production transport hypothesis: `mssql-client` 0.20.2 behind a ResourceFS-owned wrapper; pinned `sqlcmd` remains a read-only comparison oracle.
- The Database Mount discovery additions advance the Behavior Contract from 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 through optional progress fields and typed database cursors.
- This map plans and may create throwaway proof only. Production implementation belongs to a later delivery effort.

## Decisions so far

- [Select a viable Rust TDS client for the SQL Server provider](issue://rfs-7nki): conditionally take Praxiom Labs `mssql-client` 0.20.2 into the transport proof; retain `odbc-api` as fallback, Microsoft `mssql-tds` as a watch item, and pinned `sqlcmd` as a read-only oracle.
- [Prove the SQL Server TDS transport boundary](issue://rfs-w9fe): the requester approved a conditional yes on pinned SQL Server 2022; `mssql-client` passed typed values, catalog, streaming, transaction, conflict, TLS/auth, timeout/cancel, reuse, and error gates, while platform/type/pool/commit-loss gaps remain implementation and live-smoke gates.
- [Define Database Mount identity and public hierarchy](issue://rfs-i1av): `db://` is a provider-neutral navigable family from mount through uniform schema/table to one direct row-key segment, with strict canonical percent encoding, provider/catalog spelling authority, row-only mutation identity, configured-mount SQLite semantics, and provider/status metadata outside identity.
- [Define canonical row identity and JSON value semantics](issue://rfs-md8u): rows are complete catalog-order canonical JSON over a shared lossless Database Value algebra; only structurally non-null declared PK tuples form compact reversible key JSON, generated values remain tagged read-only state, post-write adapters return canonical bytes/tags, and unsupported or over-64-MiB rows fail explicitly.
- [Define database discovery search and continuation semantics](issue://rfs-mhpm): line-oriented immediate-child manifests replace database globbing; canonical-row regex search uses bounded source-ordered PK traversal and process-authenticated moving-view cursors, with metadata visibility/partial diagnostics, ADR-0006 recovery authority, page-scoped tags, and additive scan-progress fields.
- [Define transactional database mutation and concurrency semantics](issue://rfs-jr07): generated keys use a journaled table `/new` target; one-row transactions combine provider-native compare authority, exact-effect checks, authoritative reread/tag receipts, core seen-region edits, fail-closed per-verb capabilities, explicit unknown-outcome reconciliation, and the new `invalid_content` category.

## Not yet specified

## Out of scope

- Azure SQL.
- LocalDB and raw MDF attach/provisioning.
- Database providers beyond SQLite and SQL Server.
- Runtime-loaded plugins or external provider ABIs.
- Production implementation, migration, and delivery-ticket decomposition.

title: Define Atlassian operational behavior and evidence gates
description:
## Question

What operational contract should the implementation specification require for pagination ceilings, rate limits and retry guidance, caching and validators, degraded sites, stable ResourceError mapping, redaction and credential safety, deterministic fake-upstream tests, and read-only live smokes against real Jira and Confluence Cloud? Decide which ambiguities require a provisioned test tenant.

notes.content:
Resolution

### Pagination bounds

The collection contract from **Define Atlassian browse and search semantics** remains authoritative: one logical collection page is atomic and stops at 1,000 records, ten upstream requests, or the upstream terminal marker, whichever occurs first. Request sizes are fixed rather than dynamically probed:

- Jira enhanced JQL, project, issue-comment, and supported metadata/list endpoints request 100 records;
- Confluence v2 collections request 250 records;
- Confluence page-version requests carrying `body-format` request 50 records;
- Confluence v1 CQL requests 100 records and never expands bodies.

A smaller documented endpoint maximum or response-reported effective maximum wins. Terminal markers and typed continuations remain response-driven. Each endpoint is gated by documentation plus live evidence of its real clamp and continuation shape before it ships.

### Read retries and rate guidance

Only idempotent reads may retry automatically, including POST used solely for enhanced-JQL search. One logical operation gets at most one retry: after a retryable transport failure, or after 429/503 only when a valid `Retry-After` is present. `Retry-After` accepts delta-seconds and HTTP-date. ResourceFS adds 0–250 ms jitter; the full wait and retry must fit the original logical deadline. Otherwise it returns `source_unavailable` immediately.

Invalid, absent, negative, or excessive retry timing does not trigger a retry. `X-RateLimit-Reset`, beta headers, near-limit headers, and `RateLimit-Reason` are bounded diagnostics only; they never cause proactive sleeping or extend a deadline. Other 5xx responses are not retried. The no-redirect, no-retry, Unknown-outcome mutation contract remains unchanged. Retry guidance exposes only normalized delay, never raw headers.

### Cache and validator authority

Atlassian never serves stale cached content. Successful GET responses may be retained only inside the Path Session when they carry an echoable ETag. Every repeat read revalidates. A 304 may reuse the exact cached response only when its cache generation still matches. No ETag means an unconditional fetch; unreadable or oversized ETags degrade to absence; a 304 without a valid matching entry is `source_unavailable`. POST query responses are not cached.

Cache identity includes Site Mount, product, representation/Accept contract, and canonical request identity, never credentials. Successful and Unknown mutations retain the already-decided product-wide namespace invalidation, including direct, collection, and query entries.

### Degraded products and recovery

Required/optional launch probes and product-local credential degradation remain as decided in **Choose the Atlassian integration substrate and credential boundary**. This destination adds no circuit breaker and no background health worker. OAuth refresh failure remains degraded until a later bounded single-flight refresh succeeds. Ordinary transport, 5xx, and rate-limit failures are request-local and never poison a sibling product or another Site Mount.

### Stable errors and diagnostic safety

The adapter uses the stable typed matrix already established by the browse/search and mutation decisions:

- malformed local references or continuation ownership are `invalid_reference`;
- native query validation is `invalid_pattern`;
- creation/Field validation is `invalid_mutation`;
- 401, ordinary 403, and an egress-policy refusal are `permission_denied`;
- 404/410 are `not_found`;
- 413 and local hard ceilings are `limit_exceeded`;
- rate-signaled 403, 429, 5xx, transport failure, malformed upstream content/identity/continuation, unexpected endpoint redirects, and unproven conflicts are `source_unavailable`;
- `version_conflict` requires typed stale-state proof;
- cancellation is `cancelled`.

Classification uses typed status and response structure, never error-message matching. Diagnostics may expose only Site ID, product, endpoint family, stable category, HTTP status, normalized retry delay, and a bounded printable request/trace ID from an explicit header allowlist. `invalid_pattern` and `invalid_mutation` may retain bounded structured validation details. Errors, logs, caches, artifacts, Version Tags, profile reports, and stdio output never contain raw response prose, request bodies, JQL/CQL text, full URLs, account email, tokens, provider output/diagnostics, authorization/cookie headers, or other credential material.

### Deterministic evidence

Permanent CI tests use the repository's real local-TLS fake-upstream seam. They cover every route/method, endpoint clamp, offset/token/Link continuation and terminal form, the 1,000/ten-request atomic ceiling, Recovery References, malformed and cross-tenant identity/parent responses, the full status/header matrix, both Retry-After forms and deadline refusal, cache miss/revalidate/304/generation/invalidation paths, absent/corrupt validators, source/site/product degradation isolation, secret canaries, bounded diagnostics, and zero egress for rejected input. Positive controls and server-side request observations prevent vacuous passes.

### Live evidence and tenant boundary

The read milestone requires a dedicated disposable Atlassian Cloud tenant with Jira and Confluence, a provisioner/admin principal, and a separate least-privileged reader principal. A checked-in non-secret fixture manifest plus idempotent operator-run bootstrap/verify command maintains multiple projects/spaces, issues/pages/comments, ADF and storage edge cases, hierarchy, pagination, and at least one reader-concealed object. Provisioner credentials are used only for setup. Stable fixture IDs are emitted to a local ignored environment/profile file. Live tests receive reader credentials and remain GET-only.

Three ignored `live_*` rows, gated by `RFS_LIVE=1` and the required secrets, are mandatory:

1. Jira adapter: direct issue/Field/comment reads plus project and enhanced-JQL pagination.
2. Confluence adapter: direct page/Field/hierarchy/comment reads plus space and CQL pagination.
3. Stdio: generated profile → `rfs check --probe` → `rfs serve` → representative `rfs_read`/`rfs_search`, including healthy/degraded isolation and redaction invariants.

Live rows assert shapes and invariants: stable IDs, parent/container ownership, cursor/Link progression forced with explicit small limits and at least two fixtures, native media/representation shape, repeat-read identity, probe isolation, and redaction. They never assert tenant-wide counts, order without explicit sort, mutable timestamps, ETag presence, or rate exhaustion. Each run is recorded in the owning implementation ticket's `evidence.md`.

The independently shippable read milestone supports and advertises API-token authentication only. OAuth provider-command support is a later milestone and is not exposed until deterministic refresh/expiry/revocation tests plus a recorded live OAuth run pass.

Before later create/modify support ships, separately approved one-off probes against the disposable tenant must record Jira Field/comment create-update responses and immediate refetch, external-writer race behavior, Confluence page/comment version increments and stale-version response, returned stable identity/parent validation, and post-write visibility. Cleanup runs through the provisioner. Permanent live smokes stay read-only, and no test deliberately exhausts tenant rate limits.

Closed: fixed endpoint request sizes, one bounded read retry, no-stale validator caching, request-local degradation, stable error/redaction policy, deterministic fake gates, disposable-tenant topology, read-only live rows, API-token-first staging, later OAuth proof, and controlled mutation evidence are decided.
Closed: Atlassian pagination, retries, caching, degradation, errors, redaction, deterministic evidence, live tenant gates, and auth staging are decided.

title: Define canonical Atlassian site and Path Reference model
description:
## Question

What typed domain model and canonical Path Reference grammars should represent named Atlassian sites, Jira projects/issues/comments and creation targets, and Confluence spaces/pages/comments and creation targets? Decide stable canonical identity versus friendly aliases, Aggregate and Field Resource boundaries, collision handling across sites, validation rules, and catalog discovery.

notes.content:
Resolution

### Domain model

An **Atlassian Site Mount** binds one Server Profile-unique lowercase Site ID to one Atlassian Cloud tenant, one selected credential mode, independently enabled Jira and Confluence products, grants, caches, and health. `CONTEXT.md` records the canonical term. Separate validated newtypes represent the Site ID, Jira project/issue/comment IDs and aliases, Jira field IDs, Confluence space/page/comment IDs and space-key aliases, and Confluence page-version numbers. Jira and Confluence addresses are exhaustive typed sums; downstream code never reparses strings or combines flags.

### Namespace and identity

One Source Adapter owns the product-specific `jira://` and `confluence://` schemes. Every canonical object reference includes the Site ID. Jira stable object IDs are canonical nonzero decimal strings without narrowing into a machine integer. Confluence IDs remain exact bounded opaque strings. Jira project/issue keys and Confluence space keys are explicit read-only aliases; page titles are never identity. Alias reads validate the resolved stable object and return only its canonical reference. Aliases never identify mutations, snapshots, caches, continuations, search records, locks, or Version Tags.

Duplicate Site IDs and duplicate tenant authority are invalid: compare explicit OAuth cloud IDs for OAuth Site Mounts and canonical site origins for API-token Site Mounts. This prevents one upstream object acquiring two ResourceFS canonical identities through different mounts.

### Jira grammar

```text
jira://
jira://<site>
jira://<site>/projects
jira://<site>/projects/<project-id>
jira://<site>/projects/<project-id>/issues
jira://<site>/projects/<project-id>/issues/new
jira://<site>/project-keys/<project-key>
jira://<site>/issues
jira://<site>/issues/<issue-id>
jira://<site>/issue-keys/<issue-key>
jira://<site>/issues/<issue-id>/fields
jira://<site>/issues/<issue-id>/fields/<field-id>
jira://<site>/issues/<issue-id>/comments
jira://<site>/issues/<issue-id>/comments/new
jira://<site>/issues/<issue-id>/comments/<comment-id>
jira://<site>/issues/<issue-id>/comments/<comment-id>/body
```

`project-keys` and `issue-keys` are read aliases. Project issue collections link flat canonical issue references. Every visible Jira issue field has a Field Resource; the `fields` index describes its type and current mutability.

### Confluence grammar

```text
confluence://
confluence://<site>
confluence://<site>/spaces
confluence://<site>/spaces/<space-id>
confluence://<site>/space-keys/<space-key>
confluence://<site>/spaces/<space-id>/pages
confluence://<site>/spaces/<space-id>/pages/new
confluence://<site>/pages
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/title
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/body
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/version
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/versions
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/versions/<version-number>
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/ancestors
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/children
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/footer-comments
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/footer-comments/new
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/footer-comments/<comment-id>
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/footer-comments/<comment-id>/body
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/footer-comments/<comment-id>/replies
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/footer-comments/<comment-id>/replies/new
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/inline-comments
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/inline-comments/new
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/inline-comments/<comment-id>
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/inline-comments/<comment-id>/body
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/inline-comments/<comment-id>/resolved
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/inline-comments/<comment-id>/replies
confluence://<site>/pages/<page-id>/inline-comments/<comment-id>/replies/new
```

`space-keys` is a read alias. Space page collections link flat canonical page references. Comment replies also retain flat canonical comment identity; reply collections and Creation Targets nest under the parent only for navigation and creation. Historical page versions are immutable Aggregates with read-only title/body projections. `children` means direct child Pages. Unsupported direct content types are reported explicitly by type and ID rather than silently dropped or promoted into generic Resources.

### Aggregate, Field, and Creation boundaries

Site Mount, project, issue, space, current page, historical page-version, and comment Aggregates are read-only. Jira issue values use `fields/<field-id>`. Current Confluence pages expose authoritative `title` and `body`; `version` is read-only. Comment bodies are authoritative Fields. Inline comment `resolved` is readable but outside initial mutation. Stable IDs, keys, ownership, parentage, authors, and timestamps remain Aggregate metadata.

Issue creation is scoped to a stable project ID. Page creation is scoped to a stable space ID, with optional parent page identity supplied in the creation document. Comment Creation Targets are scoped to the stable owning issue/page; reply Creation Targets are additionally scoped to the stable parent comment. Reading any `/new` target returns a zero-egress local contract document describing required and optional fields, grants, `operationId`, and the canonical identity returned by a successful write.

### Validation and discovery

Site IDs are 1–63 lowercase ASCII bytes, begin and end alphanumeric, and permit only internal hyphens. Other segments reject empty values, controls, literal or encoded separators, `.`/`..`, malformed percent encoding, reserved Creation Target collisions, and values above their domain ceiling. Canonical encoding has one normalized percent-encoded spelling. Alias and opaque field/key values receive path-safety validation rather than guessed Atlassian regexes; the upstream remains authoritative.

Every upstream response is untrusted and must validate Site Mount authority, stable object identity, parent/container ownership, and collection membership before becoming a Resource.

`rfs://`, product roots, Site Mount roots, and completion derive only from validated configuration and current probe/degraded state; they perform no Atlassian egress. `rfs://` advertises each enabled product scheme. Product roots list configured Site Mounts. Site Mount roots link fixed collections, alias forms, product health, and creation guidance. Network-backed collection and search semantics remain owned by the browse/search decision.
Closed: Typed identities, canonical grammars, aliases, resource boundaries, validation, collisions, and catalog discovery are decided.

title: Define canonical row identity and JSON value semantics
description:
## Question

What provider-neutral contract makes a database row a deterministic JSON Resource across SQLite and SQL Server? Resolve supported primary and composite-key models, canonical key encoding, column ordering, missing versus null, exact encodings for numeric/date/time/GUID/binary/large and provider-specific values, generated and computed columns, unsupported-key behavior, content-derived Version Tags, and the boundary between common semantics and provider capability rejection.

notes.content:
Requester-approved resolution. One database row is a flat JSON object. Property names are exact authoritative catalog column names; properties appear once in visible catalog ordinal order. “Visible” includes normal, identity/generated, computed, and rowversion columns, but excludes SQLite virtual-module hidden=1 columns and SQL Server `is_hidden=1` engine internals. Every included property is present and SQL NULL is JSON `null`. Any included unsupported schema type makes row projection consistently `unsupported_projection`, even when the current cell is NULL; table metadata names the column/type/capability failure.

Canonical row bytes are UTF-8 with LF endings, opening/closing braces on their own lines, two-space indentation, one property/value per line, commas except after the last property, and one final newline. Column names/text emit non-control Unicode literally; quote/backslash and standard controls use the shortest JSON escapes, remaining U+0000–001F use uppercase `\u00XX`; duplicate input properties and invalid Unicode are rejected. Tagged Database Value objects are compact one-line objects with exactly one recognized key and a canonical string payload. `CONTEXT.md` now defines **Database Value** as the shared lossless value used in row bodies and keys.

The Database Value algebra is: native JSON `null`, boolean, signed integer, finite float, and text; plus `{"$decimal":"…"}`, `{"$bytes":"…"}`, `{"$uuid":"…"}`, `{"$date":"…"}`, `{"$time":"…"}`, `{"$datetime":"…"}`, `{"$datetimeOffset":"…"}`, and `{"$xml":"…"}`. Integers use JSON integer syntax. Finite float32/float64 use the shortest decimal that round-trips to the same width, force a decimal/exponent marker, and preserve `-0.0`; NaN/infinities are unsupported. Decimal has no exponent and exactly declared scale. Bytes use RFC 4648 base64url without padding. UUID is lowercase 8-4-4-4-12. Date/time/datetime use ISO forms with exactly declared fractional scale; datetimeoffset always carries explicit `+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM` and zero is `+00:00`, never `Z`. XML uses lossless authoritative provider serialization JSON-escaped onto one line, otherwise the provider rejects it. Conventional SQL JSON and SQLite JSON text remain text; SQLite JSONB remains bytes—no implicit nested-JSON parsing/retyping. SQLite values follow actual runtime storage class (NULL/signed 64-bit integer/finite binary64/text/BLOB), never declared affinity or date guessing.

Canonical row identity uses only a declared PRIMARY KEY’s complete tuple in authoritative key ordinal order; never UNIQUE, unaliased rowid, physical locator, or guessed columns. Every PK member must be structurally non-null and losslessly supported. SQLite accepts this guarantee only through `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, explicit `NOT NULL`, `STRICT`, or `WITHOUT ROWID`; ordinary nullable PK schemas are unsupported even when current data is non-null. A scalar key segment is its compact canonical Database Value JSON; a composite key is a compact canonical JSON object whose exact catalog column names appear in PK order and whose values use the same algebra. The complete bytes are percent-encoded by the settled `db://` rules. Thus integer `42`, text `"42"`, and empty text are injective. A key whose reversible canonical Path Reference exceeds 64 KiB is unaddressable with `limit_exceeded`; identity is never truncated or replaced by a digest.

Identity/generated/computed/rowversion properties are authoritative read-only values: reads include them and the Version Tag covers them; edits may echo the current value but cannot alter/assign it. Schema column addition/removal/reordering changes canonical row bytes and invalidates old tags/snapshots. The Version Tag is SHA-256 over the complete unselected canonical row bytes, including names, order, nulls, tags, read-only fields, whitespace, and final newline; selected projections retain that whole-row tag.

Write/edit input may be strict semantic JSON with different whitespace/property order/escapes, but must use unique known properties and valid fixed extension payloads. The adapter validates schema, performs the operation, re-reads generated/current values, and returns the authoritative post-write canonical row/tag. Caller formatting is never Resource state. This requires the common mutation seam to publish adapter-returned authoritative state rather than pre-hashing caller bytes; the transactional mutation ticket owns that change plus operation-specific missing/default/generated rules.

Canonical row JSON is lossless up to the existing 64 MiB artifact hard ceiling after JSON/base64 expansion. Common bounded output and Recovery References handle admissible rows; beyond the ceiling the adapter returns `limit_exceeded` with encoded size and narrowing guidance—never truncation, per-cell placeholders, or a misleading recovery link. SQL Server/SQLite aliases and provider-specific types map only when a lossless proven underlying mapping exists; `sql_variant`, spatial/CLR/UDT/encrypted/FILESTREAM/native-provider forms or transport-limited values are rejected until proven. Common `$decimal` supports the SQL exact domain, but a client unable to carry a declared precision losslessly must report unsupported capability rather than narrow it. Official facts grounding the decision: SQLite has dynamic NULL/INTEGER/REAL/TEXT/BLOB storage and nullable ordinary PK quirks (`sqlite.org/datatype3.html`, `lang_createtable.html`); SQL Server PKs are non-null and exact/approximate/temporal/binary/generated types have distinct contracts (Microsoft Learn PK, data-type, rowversion, computed-column, and maximum-capacity documentation). No additional ticket is needed: discovery/search, mutation/concurrency, configuration capabilities, and SQLite reconciliation consume this contract.

Closed: Requester approved the complete provider-neutral row object, Database Value algebra, declared-PK identity, canonical key serialization, generated-field/Version Tag semantics, post-write canonicalization, and lossless limit/unsupported behavior.

title: Define database discovery search and continuation semantics
description:
## Question

How do Database Mounts expose bounded schema/table/row discovery, listing, search, pagination, and continuation consistently across SQLite and SQL Server without pretending filesystem globbing or SQL `LIKE` equals ResourceFS search? Resolve deterministic ordering, primary-key pagination, changing-data behavior, common versus pushed-down search semantics, continuation authority, metadata visibility, table aggregates, unsupported operations, and recovery behavior under result ceilings.

notes.content:
Requester-approved resolution. Database structure discovery is owned by readable Aggregate Resources, not filesystem globbing. `db://`, mount, schema, and table reads return deterministic line-oriented manifests with stable metadata followed by immediate canonical child references only; table pages list row references, never row bodies. Each source page is bounded to 1,000 children and 64 MiB canonical manifest bytes before ordinary lower-only inline read limits/recovery apply. `rfs_glob` rejects `db://` patterns as `unsupported_projection`; no database GlobKind/source-pagination exception. Metadata-visible tables/views remain listed with object kind and capability status even when PK/value rules make row projection unsupported; their table manifest explains why.

Every readable hierarchy level may be an `rfs_search` target. An exact row searches its canonical row JSON. Table/schema/mount/family targets traverse descendant supported row Resources only—never aggregate metadata prose. The existing Rust-regex/PCRE2 engine evaluates exact canonical JSON lines locally; `caseSensitive` keeps common semantics, while SQL LIKE/full-text/collation/JSON functions do not define matches. Initial implementation performs no pattern pushdown: only explicit metadata/column selection, PK ordering, and keyset bounds reach SQL; any future coarse prefilter must prove no false negatives and locally verify candidates. `gitignore` and `hidden` options remain accepted generic fields with no Database Mount effect.

Traversal order is explicit: canonical mount/schema/table order, then each table’s complete declared PK tuple under authoritative provider type/collation semantics, then canonical row line number. Database SearchSourceResult/pages use a new validated source-order mode so core bounds/identity validation does not re-sort them; existing source normalization remains unchanged. The adapter emits at most one match record per canonical row line and owns deterministic deduplication.

Database continuations use the source target plus `:cursor:<base64url>`. The payload is versioned, self-contained, process-authenticated, bound to canonical target, mount/provider identity, traversal/table state, relevant schema/PK/collation fingerprint, and last scanned name/PK Database Values; it contains no credentials, endpoint, or SQL. It is reauthorized on every use, needs no cursor map or held connection, may cross Path Sessions in the same process/profile, and intentionally expires at process restart. Malformed/tampered/wrong-target/expired token is `invalid_reference` with restart guidance; a valid token whose bound schema/PK/collation changed is `version_conflict`. If a reversible self-contained cursor cannot fit the 64 KiB Path Reference ceiling, collection pagination fails `limit_exceeded`; exact row identity is not truncated/hashed and no stateful fallback appears.

Pagination is a documented moving-view keyset, not a cross-call snapshot. Each call uses a new short authorized read transaction strictly after the last scanned source position. Inserts before the cursor may be missed; inserts after may appear; deletes disappear; PK updates can move/duplicate/miss a row. The cursor advances after the last scanned row, never the last match. One collection-search call stops at the first of 10,000 rows examined, 64 MiB complete canonical row bytes scanned, common returned-match/result limits, source exhaustion, configured timeout, or cancellation. Server Profile/request settings may lower but never raise those scan/listing ceilings. A zero-match budget page with more rows says “No matches in this scanned page; more rows remain” and returns a cursor; only exhausted traversal says “No matches found.”

Upstream metadata visibility is authoritative: list only objects visible to the configured database principal; a guessed invisible object is `not_found`, never directly probed. Metadata-visible but data-denied exact access is `permission_denied`. Exact target failures are fatal tool errors. During broader traversal, child unsupported projection, permission denial, transient source failure, or oversized/unaddressable key becomes one ordered diagnostic and traversal continues; mount-wide connection/cancellation failures are fatal. Result structured content adds optional `scannedRecords`, `scannedBytes`, and `sourceComplete` plus text equivalents; returned/total counts are page-document counts, never whole-source totals without exhaustion. Existing `skip` counts matching records from the supplied base/cursor within bounded work; cursors are the forward-progress mechanism. This additive surface advances the Behavior Contract from 1.1.0 to 1.2.0.

ADR-0006 applies unchanged. When a source page fits inline and more source rows remain, `continuationReference` is the database cursor. If rendering overflows, `continuationReference` walks the complete artifact chain and `sourceContinuationReference` carries the database cursor; the retained document ends with the typed continuation trailer. Clients exhaust recovery first, then follow the source cursor. If omitted successful results cannot be retained under the 64 MiB artifact/session quota, the entire page fails `limit_exceeded`, publishes no artifact/cursor, and leaves prior artifacts intact—never skip unreachable matches. Cancellation threads OperationGuard through metadata/row queries, streaming, canonicalization, regex, retention, and cursor creation; it returns `cancelled`, publishes no late page/artifact/cursor, and terminates or retires an uncertain database connection.

A read-only aggregate page Version Tag is SHA-256 over the exact returned canonical page manifest, including metadata, entries, diagnostics, cursor trailer, whitespace, and final newline. It is explicitly page-scoped evidence for a moving-view read-only Aggregate Resource, never mutation authority or a claim to hash unseen collection members. No new ticket is needed: mutation consumes cursor/schema/version implications, configuration owns lower scan/time limits and principal capabilities, and SQLite reconciliation consumes the common traversal contract.

Closed: Requester approved bounded aggregate listing, no database glob, canonical-row regex search, source-order keyset cursors, moving-view consistency, visibility/diagnostic rules, ADR-0006 recovery authority, progress fields, cancellation fences, and page-scoped aggregate tags.

title: Read latest checks and commit-status Fact Resources
description:
## What to build

Deliver independent latest-check and latest-status-per-context Fact Resources for a fixed commit. Preserve actual checked SHAs and suite/collection coverage so Cyril can interpret freshness without ResourceFS producing a review verdict.

User stories covered: 26–27, 28–38. Shared applicable safety/proof stories are included in every slice. Story 44 is the approved breakdown/publication process, not an implementation feature.

Source: GitHub Fact Resource contract specification in the sibling resourcefs-wt-github-resource-contract documentation worktree (docs/github-resource-contract-spec.md). User approved this eight-slice breakdown and dependency graph. Exact grammar/schema spellings marked PROPOSED remain subject to the specification's applicable design approval gate; issue creation does not waive that gate or authorize live tenant operations.

Shared contract (mandatory for every applicable path): existing public SourceAdapter/SourceResource; owned versioned /facts JSON, not private wire DTOs or Markdown scraping; unchanged human projections and five tools. ResourceFS owns acquisition; Cyril owns capture authorization/totals, retention, UI and review meaning. One configured deployment, explicit repository/fork/origin authority, embedder-supplied origin-bound credentials, new Path Session on principal change, REST 2022-11-28, validated selected ghe.com web/API pairing; no new sign-in flow or provider framework.

Preserve deployment/source identity, supplied native repository/object IDs and links, requested versus observed immutable operands, acquisition interval and REST version, supplied upstream versions/times separately, missing/null/unknown values and explicit coverage. VersionTag hashes representation bytes, not Git identity. Reuse the first slice's reviewed envelope and error vocabulary; additive optional fields permitted, unsupported major versions rejected. Keep one ResourceError with stable categories and bounded sanitized structured status/access ambiguity/retry/limit details; no message parsing, hidden-404-to-empty or denial-to-expired-login inference.

Per-read measurement targets: 10 physical attempts including parent lookups/revalidation/retries; 30 seconds shared across send/body/wait; 8 MiB per response; 16 MiB cumulative accepted response bodies; 16 MiB serialized JSON INCLUDING provenance/outcome/continuation; 4 MiB decoded regular-file bytes; 1,000 records per collection. Positive lower-only acquisition controls are separate from display limits: reject zero/above-hard-ceiling inputs and intersect valid requests with operator policy. These are not memory or wire-traffic guarantees. Measure implementation feasibility; do not silently raise ceilings. Reuse bounded retry/cache behavior and honor applicable rate guidance within the same deadline; failed revalidation cannot return stale success.

Collections admit whole verified pages only if all record/body/serialized budgets fit. Ordinary later failures preserve valid earlier pages with honest coverage, and continuation ONLY when valid; continuation is NOT required for retention. First failure without usable data is typed failure, not empty success. Cancellation or authority/requested-identity violations reject the current component including acquired pages. Continuations are credential-free, session-scoped and resource/operand/authority-bound; best-effort traversal, not snapshots. Expose provider caps separately; no invented recovery or exhaustive fallback to hide caps.

## Placement / boundaries

resourcefs-core owns fixed-commit CI resource grammar. resourcefs-sources GitHub owns private checks/status/suite decoding, latest selection and bounded coverage projection. resourcefs-mcp uses existing read/catalog/recovery. Reuse slice 4 immutable addressing and slice 2 collections; no polling/orchestration, history/log/artifact downloader, app authentication or review-freshness module.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Checks preserve native run/suite/app/source IDs, requested and actual checked SHA, name/external ID/status/nullable conclusion, supplied times and links; missing facts remain explicit.
- [ ] Statuses select latest per context and retain native ID/source/creator/state/description/times/links and actual checked SHA. Combined state/count are separate facts; pending with no statuses does not mean running.
- [ ] Latest selection is verified against independent provider history/order, not first fixture row. Retain distinct native contexts/sources and do not claim historical coverage.
- [ ] Acquire suite information needed for latest-run coverage within the same budget; expose suite caps, inaccessible/unenumerated suites and local exhaustion. One successful list is not all CI.
- [ ] After a push, requested versus actual checked revision remains visible: no automatic revision switch, current/green/safe verdict or empty-success fallback. Empty complete differs from incomplete/inaccessible.
- [ ] Checks/statuses are independent reads with shared collection safeguards; no historical attempts, logs, downloadable artifacts, dispatch or remote writes.
- [ ] Complete this Resource path through validated addressing, configured Source Adapter acquisition/projection, catalog grammar/examples, applicable profile/CLI schema/check integration, public library consumption and real MCP read/recovery. No private inspector, new tool/provider trait or duplicate HTTP client.
- [ ] Independently observe expected upstream requests, requested/observed identities, zero forbidden egress and zero remote writes, including failure/retry/cancellation. Exercise applicable exact/over-limit controls, shared attempts/deadline, sanitized errors, partial retention and integrity overrides. Existing human reads retain their meaning.
- [ ] Library consumers parse complete bounded JSON; real MCP Recovery References reconstruct exactly acquired JSON before parsing. Source continuation is separately upstream acquisition under ADR-0006, not recovery of omitted output.
- [ ] Add applicable ignored live_* read-only smokes for new adapter and primary real rfs stdio paths, gated by RFS_LIVE=1 and GITHUB_TOKEN, skipping cleanly when absent. Record executed evidence and exact revision in the owning issue evidence record; use public/authorized controlled upstream shapes and invariants, not moving counts. Skipped rows are not passes.
